News.title: Fury as pub puts up huge AI mural full of mistakes leaving local artists ‘insulted’ – can you spot the errors?
News.content:
'SOULLESS PLAIGIARISM' Fury as pub puts up huge AI mural full of mistakes leaving local artists ‘insulted’ – can you spot the errors?







Next

A PUB has sparked fury after putting up a huge AI mural full of mistakes leaving locals and neighbouring artists “insulted” – but can you spot the errors?

The large vinyl sticker was pasted onto the side of the Jolly Colliers pub on Wednesday in Bedminster, Bristol.



Given the city’s international reputation for street art and its strong connections to Banksy, the decision to use artificial intelligence to design the piece was met with immediate criticism.

The area is also famous for hosting Upfest, Europe’s largest street art festival.



The bizarre artwork mangled almost every Bristol landmark it attempted to depict.

This included a botched imitation of Banksy’s Mild Mild West that showed a one-legged figure pointing rather than the famous teddy bear throwing a petrol bomb.

Other glaring errors included an inaccurate version of Cabot Tower and Isambard Kingdom Brunel’s SS Great Britain, which was rendered looking more like a tugboat.

The image featured a fictional viaduct-style bridge over water, even though the only nearby equivalent, the Pensford viaduct, sits in Somerset and does not cross water.

Traffic flow was also overlooked by the algorithm, which depicted all cars crossing the Clifton Suspension Bridge travelling in the exact same direction despite it being a two-lane road.

In the top-left corner, a neo-Gothic structure appeared to scramble features from several distinct landmarks.



The AI debacle merged the Wills Memorial, Bristol Cathedral, and St Mary Redcliffe into a single building.

A row of colourful houses was positioned on the west side of the Clifton Suspension Bridge.

But the real-life properties are actually situated on the opposite side of the city in Cliftonwood, overlooking the harbour.



On Tuesday, a letter from an unknown artist condemning the artwork was placed below the mural, calling it “a disrespectful affront to this city”.

The letter also slammed the AI work as “an insult” to capable creatives.

It said: “I am not alone in this opinion. Your decisions have angered a large portion of the very community you supposedly wish to support and exist alongside.”

The letter continued: “You have watered down the spirit, the originality and the very essence of the visual aesthetic you have tried, and failed, to recreate.”

It added the depiction is “riddled with glaring mistakes”, including “invented” buildings.



Caroline Maggs, of Bristol Mural Collective (BMC), told the magazine Bristol 24/7 that “AI designs not only devalue, but undermine the work of artists” and that the collective was “saddened and angered by the Jolly Colliers not choosing to support handmade work”.

Ms Maggs continued: “We are small businesses, and as a small business themselves, they should have chosen better.

“In a climate where humans are being replaced by AI at an alarming rate, choosing art like this is not only an aesthetic choice, but a political one.”

The AI mural has now been removed after huge backlash in Bristol.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesman from Punch, which owns the pub, said the mural was “a temporary measure due to the condition of the external wall” and they were looking forward to collaborating with local artists for a permanent mural.



They added: “The external wall requires some minor works, which would make a permanent mural at this time difficult, so we have opted for a temporary solution.”

News.title: We’ve had our fill of lame excuses as to why Labour can’t stop the boats – Burnham must now deliver a realistic plan
News.content:
Stop the hopes







Next

WE’VE suspected it for some time and yesterday we heard it straight from a Cabinet minister’s mouth.

Labour has effectively given up all hope of stopping the boats. The mood at the heart of government was summed up by one of Andy Burnham’s closest allies on another record day for migrant crossings.



Asked to explain how two migrant boats reached the Kent coast without interception, Lucy Powell sighed: “You can’t stop everything all of the time.”

Her words reflect the Government’s defeatist attitude toward Britain’s broken borders crisis.



Nearly 800 illegal migrants crossed the Channel in ten boats on Wednesday — the most in a single day this year. In a further embarrassment, two dinghies managed to reach the Kent coast without being intercepted.

Burnham took office promising to be “relentless” in tackling the problem.

Yet since Labour won power, 83,279 people have made the perilous crossing — outnumbering the full-time ranks of the British Army.

We’ve had our fill of lame excuses and fatalistic shrugs of the shoulder.

The PM must deliver a realistic plan — and stop yielding to defeat.

Hooky street

EVIL hate preacher Abu Hamza has taken soft-touch Britain for a ride for too long.



For years, the hook-handed bile- monger was allowed to inspire wannabe terrorists openly on the streets while his family lived rent-free on benefits.

His days of spreading poison may be over as he serves a life sentence in a US supermax prison, but he continues to play us for fools from behind bars.

Taxpayers will be forced to foot the bill for a £70,000 refurbishment of the five-bedroom council home where his wife still lives in Shepherd’s Bush.

Families in need of a house of that size in the same London borough face a wait of five to six years. It’s little wonder so many undesirables flock to our shores.

Hamza, who once described Britain as “the inside of a toilet”, has treated the authorities like mugs long enough.



It’s time to send a clear message to anyone who despises this country: sling your hook.

Left for dread

A BOMBSHELL poll exposes the terrifying prospect of Britain being ruled by a rabble alliance of the hard Left.

The survey predicts Labour would win most seats if an election were held today — but 85 short of an outright majority.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It raises the nightmare scenario of the party forming a coalition of chaos with the Lib Dems, Greens and nationalists.

Tories might wish to sleep on that when they next consider ruling out a “unite the right” pact with Reform.

News.title: Kemi’s ‘tough love’ for the workshy doesn’t go far enough… here’s my plan to get ALL the long-term unemployed into work
News.content:
Next

BRAVO to Kemi Badenoch for ­promising some much-needed “tough love” to get the long-term jobless back into work.

But I’m sorry to say the Tory leader’s bid to end the right to idleness at the taxpayers’ expense doesn’t go nearly far enough.



Mrs Badenoch has announced a pledge to slash benefits for some unemployed people on Universal Credit and to block them from spending their welfare cash on booze, fags and gambling.

All well and good so far.



Under her plans, anyone who claims UC when they are unemployed who hasn’t previously worked and contributed taxes for years would get six months of full benefits to find a job — but would then see their payments slashed by 30 per cent.

That lower payment would also be loaded on to a “Back To Work” pre- payment card that would prevent spending on alcohol, cigarettes, betting and cash withdrawals.

This eye-catching initiative has upset the usual suspects, who’ve bleated about how it shames welfare claimants by telling them what they can and cannot spend their money on.

This rather misses the whole point, which is that the jobless aren’t being told how they can spend THEIR money; they’re being told how they can spend OUR money.

If you want to splash your own hard-earned cash in the pub or at the bookies, that’s up to you.

But if you’re living off everyone else’s taxes, then we have every right to demand that you don’t fritter our money away on cigarettes and alcohol.



While many are asking, “Why didn’t the Tories do this when they were in power?”, others are wondering, “Will they actually go through with it if they are ever back in charge?”

These are both reasonable ­questions. But I want to add another: Do these proposals really go far enough?

Kemi Badenoch estimates these changes would affect 350,000 of the 1.1million ­Universal Credit claimants who are out of work and required to be looking for a job, and would save taxpayers about £538million a year.

That might sound like a lot of money, but, in reality, that saving is a tiny drop in the ocean of the total cost of Universal Credit, which is set to hit a whopping £88BILLION this year. Indeed, it’s not even one hundredth of the total cost.

While most people who lose their jobs quickly find another one, far too many — and especially the young — now see ­claiming benefits as a perfectly reasonable lifestyle choice.



So, wouldn’t it make more sense for Kemi Badenoch (and the other party ­leaders) to go much further?

Why only a 30 per cent cut to benefits after six months? Why not time-limited benefits for ALL job-seekers and a 100 per cent cut, with a zero-tolerance policy on school and college leavers who have never done a day’s work in their lives?

That’s the real tough love this nation needs. And it will save us a fortune, too.



Of course, those who have worked and paid taxes for years should be treated with dignity and respect if they lose their job, but young people should expect to pay in before they get any payout. That means parents who don’t want their layabout offspring living as freeloading lodgers for life had better start ­teaching their kids what a work ethic is.

We are constantly being told that it’s hard to find work and yet most ­people who want to work DO find jobs. And, even with rising ­unemployment, the Government is still busy importing hundreds of thousands of workers from abroad to do all the jobs we’re told Brits refuse to do. So, let’s stop offering them that option.

If people can’t find a job after six months, then the State will step in and find one for you.

It may not be your dream job but, hey, beggars can’t be choosers!

And if you refuse that job, then your benefits are stopped.



If you take the job but then don’t turn up every day, on time, and end up getting sacked, then you will have to live with the consequences.

Ensuring that people keep the dignity, self-respect and the daily routine of going to work is a far kinder policy than leaving people to rot on their sofas watching ­daytime telly for years on end.

Will a strict time limit on benefits see people starving on the streets?

Of course not. Even the laziest able- ­bodied benefit scrounger still makes ­rational decisions. When they’re hungry and cold enough, they’ll get a job.

This is the real world. The one that everyone else lives and works in every day, while we fund a burgeoning benefit class that plays by different rules, aided and abetted by the handwringing liberal lanyard-wearers.



So by all means, let’s have some tough love for benefit claimants.

But let’s make sure it’s tough enough to do the job of cutting our welfare bill and getting them back into work.

REJOIN? EU MUST BE JOKING

BRITAIN should rejoin the EU in the next decade, Sir Tony Blair has urged.

Of course he has. It’s a day with a Y in it, after all.

The former PM has called on Andy Burnham to make overturning Brexit part of his ten-year plan in November, suggesting it is in our interests to rejoin “a reformed Europe”.



Sir Tony and his fellow Remoaners are never going to accept the 2016 vote for Brexit.

But why Blair and his ilk think rejoining the failing European bloc is the answer to all our ills is beyond me. For some utterly incomprehensible reason, they are convinced that Brexit is responsible for everything that’s gone wrong with the country since. Forget Covid lockdowns, the impacts of the Ukraine War and the conflict in the Middle East or the influx of millions of low-wage migrants and a ballooning welfare bill.

No, apparently our economic woes are all the fault of some extra paperwork and passport queues at Dover. Burnham has not ruled out putting a vote to rejoin the EU in the next Labour manifesto.

And, as a diehard Brexiteer, I hope he DOES make that election pledge. Why?

Because there is more chance of the British people voting to rejoin the Roman empire than there is of a vote to go on our hands and knees to Brussels to beg them to take us back.



The EU wouldn’t be able to resist offering us punishing terms: many billions more in membership payments, with Margaret Thatcher’s rebate long gone, with free movement, a requirement that we take many thousands of their illegal immigrants and, of course, we would have to ditch the Pound and join the euro.

Anyone who thinks that the British people are going to vote for any of that must be out of their tiny minds.

That glorious June morning ten years ago when I woke to a Leave victory is still one of the best days of my life, and I’d be happy to add another one to that list.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bring it on!

News.title: ‘Crazy’ Freeview TV switch off is ‘threat to national security’ blasts ex-Defence Secretary
News.content:
Next

FORMER Defence Secretary Penny Mordaunt says the plan to switch off Freeview TV is a threat to national security.

She says it is a vital method of communication during war if the enemy knocks out digital-only telly — which comes via internet broadband.



Ms Mordaunt said: “It is crazy that we are still considering ditching the main method of public information should the internet be inoperative.”

Sir Gavin Williamson, another former Defence Secretary, said: “When the internet fails, through accident or attack, it is how the Government will warn the nation.”



Shadow Culture Secretary Rebecca Paul added: “Ministers should not even be contemplating switching off the one network that reaches every home when the internet fails until they have explained the workable alternative they would replace it with.”

A poll shows 82 per cent would turn to radio or Freeview TV if internet networks failed.

Ministers are consulting on a 2034 or 2044 switch off for terrestrial TV.

However, Andy Burnham indicated last month he was concerned about the switch-off which has come up as an issue in his Greater Manchester constituency.

He said: “I am concerned about those plans too.

“I know some of my constituents in Makerfield rely on Freeview.



“There is perhaps an opportunity to look at this as part of the BBC Charter renewal process…. I recognise it’s a genuine issue…I know it will be of concern to constituents and let me have a proper look at it”

Our Save Our Sets campaign aims to protect free TV.

News.title: Hard-right activist Danny Tommo charged with criminal damage after he ‘slashed migrant dinghy in Channel’
News.content:
ACTIVIST CHARGE Hard-right activist Danny Tommo charged with criminal damage after he ‘slashed migrant dinghy in Channel’







Next

HARD-RIGHT activist Danny Tommo has been charged after allegedly being filmed slashing a boat in the English Channel with a rescue crew member on board.

Tommo, whose real name is Daniel Thomas, 37, has been charged with criminal damage and failing to disclose the PIN to his phone, Hampshire Police said.



The charges come after footage appeared to show Thomas attacking a boat with a blade.

A rescue crew member was reportedly on board at the time of the incident in the Channel.



Thomas, also known as Danny Tommo, was arrested by cops yesterday evening.

He remains in custody following the charges and is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court tomorrow morning.

Chris Derrick from the Crown Prosecution Service said: “The Crown Prosecution Service has decided to prosecute Daniel Thomas following an investigation by Hampshire Constabulary into an incident on Tuesday 22 September.

“Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and that it is in the public interest to pursue criminal proceedings.

“We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and he has the right to a fair trial.”

A video shared yesterday appears to show the moment Tommo was arrested at a BP petrol station last night.



The 37-year-old was pounced on by cops as unmarked police cars surrounded the vehicle he was in.

Dramatic footage uploaded to his YouTube channel appears to show the moment officers swooped on him.

Tommo can be seen getting out of his car as police approach.

He can then be heard saying: “Yep okay, okay, if I can just speak to my kids, I’m trying to say goodbye to my kids.”

An officer tells him: “At this moment in time we have information to suggest that you have been involved in criminal damage.”



Another officer can then be heard saying: “Let’s go, let’s go” as Tommo is placed in handcuffs.

The arrest came after cops began investigating an incident in the Channel in which a dinghy was allegedly slashed with a blade while a rescue worker was onboard.

The boat had been carrying around 50 migrants who launched from a beach in Normandy.

They were picked up by two RNLI lifeboats after reaching the UK search and rescue area before being transferred to a Border Force vessel and taken to Dover.

Tommo had been filming the transfer from a yellow speedboat while giving a running commentary to a live-stream audience of more than 15,000.



The footage then appears to show him sailing towards the dinghy, taking out a small knife and slashing at its side.

There were no migrants on board at the time, but a French official from the coastguard vessel Abeille Liberté was present.

In another video, Tommo appeared to shout “traitors” as he cut into the inflatable vessel.

He appears to have targeted the boat after a rescue crew member had boarded it to apparently take it back to France.

Tommo, who founded anti-migration group Patriot Platform, also appeared to film his own arrest.



During the footage, he asks police if he can use his phone to speak to his children.

One officer says: “The information that I’ve been given… is that you’ve been involved in criminal damage recklessly endangering someone’s life.”

Thomas repeatedly replies: “I understand.”

News.title: Fuming Met boss slams courts for repeatedly bailing sex offender to his home overlooking children’s playground
News.content:
BAILED AND FAILED Fuming Met boss slams courts for repeatedly bailing sex offender to his home overlooking children’s playground







Next

BRITAIN’S top cop has blasted the justice system after a paedo was repeatedly bailed to his home overlooking a playground.

Zafer Dogan, 32, took more than 5,000 photos of unsuspecting kids and adults then turned them into explicit content using AI.

Police and the CPS opposed bail three times after the mechanic was charged in August of making indecent images of children.



But each time the courts freed him back to his home, despite many of the pictures being taken from his bedroom window in Enfield, North London.



One of his victims and their family were forced to move home because he lived nearby.

After Dogan was jailed for 28 months yesterday, Met Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley, said: “It is not often you will see me outside court following a sentencing.

“But this is yet another example of victims being let down by a criminal justice system that too often fails to put their safety first — in this case children.

“That is simply not acceptable, the children should have been put first, not the paedophile.”

He said angry and upset officers are flagging “ever increasing volumes of cases” to him when they feel “hamstrung by a justice system that makes seemingly unfathomable decisions”.

Sir Mark also criticised tech firms for allowing their platforms and tools to be used for sex offending.

Dogan, who admitted all offences including making indecent images of a child in the most severe category, was also given a Sexual Harm Prevention order at Wood Green crown court and was placed on the sex offenders’ register for ten years.

News.title: ‘Assassins were sent to kill Costa del Sol diner but murdered innocent man, 20,’ days before football ultra shot in face
News.content:
BLOODY FUED ‘Assassins were sent to kill Costa del Sol diner but murdered innocent man, 20,’ days before football ultra shot in face







Next

ASSASSINS sent to kill a Turkish football ultra holidaying in Spain shot dead an innocent man just days before the Malaga bloodbath, it has been reported.

Ümit Yalçın, 47, is fighting for his life after being shot in the face while having dinner on the marina, sparking a mass manhunt.



Police are investigating whether the attack is linked with the killing of Nacho Ignacio, 20, in the La Victoria district.

A team of three men, who are believed to have travelled from Sweden, mistook him for a member of a rival gang as he smoked at a cafe at the same time every day.



He was shot twice in the back and taken to hospital, but he could not be saved.

One of the suspects was apprehended shortly after the incident with a weapon, while the other two were detained at different addresses, local media have reported.

A second team of assassins was then deployed to take out their original target Yalçın, Halk TV alleged.

Footage from the night of the attack shows the Turkish national lying on the ground with blood on the back of his white shorts.

He is said to be in a serious but stable condition in hospital.

Known as “Gypsy Ümit,” Yalçın is a prominent leader within the notorious ultra supporter base of Turkish club Fenerbahçe SK.



He is credited as a founding member of Genç Fenerbahçeliler (GFB), a hooligan group with a long history of violence, street-gang rivalries and criminal prosecutions.

In 2016, Yalçın survived a drug-related gang attack when his companion shielded him.

In recent years, his name has been particularly associated with alleged drug trafficking and land grabs in Istanbul’s districts.



Spanish police are yet to confirm a link between the two cases in Malaga.

“A man, born in 1979, was shot in the face and was subsequently taken to a hospital in Malaga,” said a statement from the force.

“The National Police have opened an investigation aimed at clarifying the circumstances of the incident.

“At present, no arrests have been made.”

News.title: Brit airport owner killed in Swiss Alps plane crash alongside pals as family pay tribute to ‘incredible dad’
News.content:
ALPS TRAGEDY Brit airport owner killed in Swiss Alps plane crash alongside pals as family pay tribute to ‘incredible dad’







Next

AN AIRPORT owner and businessman has been named as one of three people killed when a plane crashed into a mountain in the Swiss Alps.

Anthony Hall, known as Tony, was described as an “incredible dad” and “truly wonderful husband” by his heartbroken family.



The 42-year-old owned Wolverhampton Halfpenny Green Airport in Staffordshire and was managing director of construction and recycling firm Pegasus.

He died on September 15 when the Cirrus SR22T he was travelling in smashed into a mountain slope near the resort town of Leukerbad.



Tony’s family said they were “completely heartbroken” by the loss of their loved one.



In a statement, they said: “Tony was an exceptional businessman who achieved great things in the construction/haulage industry, and his commitment to succeed and progress never faltered.

“He was first and foremost a loving husband and an incredible dad to his daughter, whose family meant everything to him.



“We will miss him immensely and will remember him as the kind, caring, generous, determined and fantastic character he was.”

The light aircraft had taken off from Sion Airport in the Rhône Valley before crashing into a northern mountain slope around ten minutes later.

Emergency crews, including police, firefighters and rescue teams, raced to the scene along with three helicopters.

All three people on board were killed.

Businessman Owain Davies, 55, from west Wales, was previously identified as another Briton killed in the horror crash.



The Swiss Transportation Safety Investigation Board has launched an investigation into the tragedy.

Tony bought Wolverhampton Halfpenny Green Airport in 2023 and had a vision of turning it into “the best general aviation airport in the country”.

In a tribute, the airport said he had “poured his time, energy and passion” into securing its future.

It added: “Together with his co-owner, he transformed the airport, creating a thriving aviation hub for the local and wider aviation community.”

Tony was also remembered by former Stourbridge MP Suzanne Webb, who described him as “one of the very best”.



She said: “Tony will always be a legend to me.

“What he achieved in helping build Pegasus into the success it is today, alongside the other directors, was remarkable.

“But beyond the business, Tony was great fun to be around and, quite simply, a genuinely good person. I will miss his quick wit and humour.”

Ms Webb also praised Tony for giving “so much” to the local area, particularly through his support for the Poppy Appeal and Military Vehicle Parade.

She said: “Having served in the armed forces, he gave his support willingly.



“His life was tragically cut short, but what he achieved after leaving the army was truly inspiring, and he did it with a passion I was always in awe of.”

Pegasus also paid tribute to its managing director, saying there was “immense sadness” over his death.

A spokesperson said: “He built a strong team and a business with values and solid foundations, which he was incredibly proud of.”

The firm added it would continue operating as normal, “just as Tony would have wanted”.

“Above everything else, Tony was a much-loved husband, father, friend, and colleague,” the spokesperson said.



“He will be deeply missed.”

Tony’s family thanked everyone who had shown them “kindness, love and support” since his death.

They said: “Our hearts go out to those who also lost their lives in this terrible tragedy.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They asked for privacy as they came to terms with their loss.

The Foreign Office has confirmed it is supporting the families of two British nationals who died in Switzerland and remains in contact with local authorities.

News.title: Family's heartbreaking plea 26 years after Vicky Glass found murdered in stream
News.content:
Family's heartbreaking plea 26 years after Vicky Glass found murdered in stream

Detectives have examined hundreds of hours of CCTV footage and made several arrests over the years, but the mystery surrounding Vicky Glass's murder remains unsolved more than two decades later

View 4 Images Vicky's body was discovered in a stream near Danby, North Yorkshire, six weeks after she disappeared (Image: Evening Gazette)

The family of a young woman murdered just days after turning 21 have renewed their desperate search for answers — after her heartbroken mum died without ever knowing who killed her daughter.

‌



Vicky Glass vanished in Middlesbrough, Teesside, in the early hours of September 24, 2000. Six weeks later, her body was discovered in a stream on North Yorkshire moorland, around 20 miles from where she was last seen. Now, 26 years on, her devastated family have vowed to continue fighting for justice, revealing how they mourn her every day and grieve for the woman she never had the chance to become.

‌



In an emotional statement, Vicky's family said: "We have spoken about our pain year after year, how can we emphasise that this pain increases as the time goes on. It is vicious and brutal. It breaks us down, but it will never stop us from fighting for Vicky, to keep asking for your help, to get answers, to get justice for Vicky."

‌



View 4 Images Police released CCTV footage in 2022 in the hope of uncovering new leads (Image: Evening Gazette)

Sister's heartbreak as Brit brother disappears abroad leaving family desperate for answers READ MORE :

Victims of Nuked Blood scandal meet with Andy Burnham in Downing Street READ MORE :

Despite four arrests over the years, nobody has ever been charged with Vicky's murder. Her mother, Deborah, died without discovering who was responsible for her daughter's death.

The family said: "Our grief intensifies, it's not only grieving her life being taken, we grieve for the woman she could have been if she was still here with us, the chance for change was ripped from her. We grieve for our family, for who we could have been, a family with Vicky with us.

‌



"We mourn every single day, not being able to talk to her, go shopping with her, sitting around a table with her having a family meal, laughing with her, making memories with her, all the small things that are taken for granted we do not have. We were not given that chance."

Vicky was last seen at around 4am on Union Street in Middlesbrough, near its junction with Eshwood Square, after being dropped off by a taxi driver. Her body was found in horrific condition due to the decomposition after it was pulled from the river and was found near the village of Danby on November 3, 2000.

View 4 Images In 2021, a detailed review of the original murder investigation was carried out after it failed to find Vicky's murderer. The review included that a reinvestigation should be undertaken. (Image: Evening Gazette)

‌



Detectives have examined more than 200 hours of CCTV footage during the investigation. Three people were arrested in previous years, while a fourth suspect, a 65-year-old man, was arrested in June this year and remains on police bail. Officers have also sought information about a lorry driver believed to have spoken to Vicky before she disappeared.

Vicky turned to sex work to fuel her crippling drug habit. In 2022, Cleveland Police released CCTV footage showing Vicky, who was a sex worker, with a friend. She was wearing light-coloured trousers and a top, white trainers and a dark puffer-style jacket. After speaking to her friend, detectives learned that Vicky had spoken to a lorry driver who gave her money. Police said she left personal belongings with him and agreed to meet him again later that day.

The driver was described as a white man with a broad build and a distinctive mole on his face. He was believed to have been aged between 34 and 38 at the time.

‌



On 8 August 2003 at an inquest into the woman’s death Dr Kenneth Shorrock delivering a post-mortem examination and said he was unable to give a pathological cause of Vicky’s death. The doctor described the difficulties he had in examining the badly decomposed body. In a grim revelation Dr Shorrock revealed numerous parts of Glass's body were missing – including a number of her major organs and bones.

At the inquest coroner Michael Oakley said: "We don't know how she came to be where she was found, we don't know the cause of death as whether there was a third party directly or indirectly involved in her death."

View 4 Images Vicky's loved ones have vowed never to give up their fight for justice (Image: Evening Gazette)

‌



As police continue to investigate the unsolved murder, Vicky's family have spoken of their anguish at knowing the person responsible has yet to face justice. They said: "For 26 years we have been waiting for the cold-blooded monster that murdered Vicky to be named, for justice to be served, for them to pay the price for what they have done.

"For 26 years this killer has lived a life they had no right to live, a life free of consequence with no thought for the life they stole our Vicky's life and our lives."

Detective Chief Inspector Steve Chatterton, who is leading the investigation for Cleveland Police, urged anyone with information about Vicky's movements between her disappearance and the discovery of her body to contact officers.

‌



He said: "Vicky’s family have longed for answers regarding her death and the person responsible for 26 years. As we continue to investigate Vicky’s murder, we would again appeal for anyone with information regarding Vicky’s whereabouts, between the last sighting of her and her body being found six weeks later, to contact us.

"Any information at all could assist us in finally bringing to justice the person who murdered Vicky Glass, and bringing an end to this nightmare for her family."

In a final appeal, her family said: "Our lives are plagued, there is a dark shadow that follows us, we can't get justice for Vicky on our own so we ask once again, we implore anyone with any information, big or small, to please come forward."

Article continues below

Anyone with information can contact Cleveland Police on 101 or the dedicated inquiry line on 01642 301773. Information can also be passed anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Brit, 21, died 'in company of stranger' after purchase from online poison seller
News.content:
Brit, 21, died 'in company of stranger' after purchase from online poison seller

Aimee Louise Elif Walton, 21, is one of 79 victims from the UK known to have died as a direct result of purchasing poison from Canadian national Kenneth Law

View 3 Images Aimee Louise Elif Walton, from Southampton (Image: Walton Family/PA Wire)

A British victim of a Canadian national who shipped lethal substances to people across the world “died in the company of a stranger met online”, her sister has told a court.

‌



Aimee Louise Elif Walton, from Southampton, was found dead in a hotel room on October 14 2022.

‌



The 21-year-old is one of 79 victims from the UK known to have died as a direct result of purchasing poison from Kenneth Law, who sold 1,200 packages to 40 countries across the world from Canada-based websites.

‌



Law, 61, previously pleaded guilty to 14 counts of aiding suicide, all relating to Canadian victims.

Although Law was not formally charged with the deaths, the 79 UK victims also form part of the wider Canadian case into his offending.

View 3 Images Kenneth Law (pictured left) is being sentenced (Image: Arlyn McAdorey/The Canadian Pres)

‌



Families whose loved ones were 'groomed' into suicide demand Andy Burnham launch public inquiry READ MORE :

No justice for student who died after taking poison bought online, father says READ MORE :

Ms Walton’s sister, Adele Zeynep Walton, recorded her victim impact statement in a video which was played out in court in Ontario, Canada, on Thursday.

In her statement, Adele Walton said her sister was not found by a friend, as previously reported, but died in the company of a stranger she had met in an internet forum where people discussed ending their own lives.

The man “had flown from America to be with her when she died”, and had been staying with her for 11 days prior to her death, Adele Walton said.

‌



“She died in a strange place, in a strange city, in the company of a stranger,” Adele Walton told the court.

“You only need to listen to the recording of the emergency call to know how much she suffered during the last moments of her life.”

Ms Walton purchased poison from Law for a total of 269 dollars (£203) on several occasions between June 2022 and September 2022.

‌



View 3 Images Aimee with singer Pharrell Williams, who she was a big fan of (Image: Adele Walton)

She had been struggling with her mental health since the Covid-19 pandemic, which resulted in her delaying her studies, Adele Walton told the court.

Authorities previously informed the victims’ families that Law would not face criminal proceedings in the UK because of the potential for the hotel cook to challenge the extradition under “double jeopardy” laws.

‌



This means a court could technically refuse extradition on the basis that Law had already been convicted of similar offences in another country.

Adele Walton, along with other family members of the British victims, previously criticised the decision, saying “doors have been shut” for families seeking justice.

“The question for our own country is simpler still: who here will examine how the British state let this happen, and what it will do so that no other family goes through it?” Adele Walton previously said.

‌



“A foreign sentencing hearing cannot answer that. Only a statutory public inquiry can.”

It has been established Law sent a total 330 products to the UK, with 286 individuals receiving the products, according to the NCA.

The court previously heard Law was the sole owner of four companies, with one firm’s website offering a “set of instructions” and advertising 40-minute telephone consultations for 150 dollars (£111).

‌



The court in Ontario also heard how Law would occasionally frequent an online forum where users discussed ending their lives and he would post under the pseudonym “Greenberg” to direct people to one of his websites.

The maximum sentence for aiding suicide in Canada is 14 years – the same for encouraging suicide in the UK.

It is understood that the sentence in this case is likely to be more than 14 years because of the number of victims and the nature of the offences.

Article continues below

For mental health support, contact the Samaritans on 116 123, email them at jo@samaritans.org or visit samaritans.org to find your nearest branch.

News.title: Far-right activist Daniel 'Tommo' Thomas charged after 'slashing dinghy in Channel'
News.content:
Far-right activist Daniel 'Tommo' Thomas charged after 'slashing dinghy in Channel'

Danny 'Tommo' Thomas has been charged by police with criminal damage after he allegedly slashed a dinghy in the English Channel

View 2 Images Danny 'Tommo' Thomas has been charged (Image: Jonathan Buckmasterr)

Far-right activist Danny 'Tommo' Thomas has been charged after a video was shared that allegedly showed him slashing a dinghy in the Channel.

Thomas, 37, an associate of anti-immigration activist Tommy Robinson, previously uploaded footage onto his YouTube channel that appeared to show the moment he was arrested by police. He was seen getting out of his vehicle as officers approached him.

Hampshire Constabulary this evening confirmed he has been charged with one count of criminal damage. He was also charged with failing to disclose the Pin to his phone to police, under Section 53 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.

He was remanded into custody to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court on Friday, Hampshire police said.

Hampshire Police said: "A man has been charged in connection with an incident that occurred in the English Channel on Tuesday 22 September.

View 2 Images People gathered outside a police investigation centre in Basingstoke this evening, believing that Thomas was inside (Image: Getty Images)

"Daniel Thomas, aged 37 and of no fixed abode, has been charged with one count of criminal damage. He has also been charged with a further offence under Section 53 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 (RIPA), for allegedly failing to comply with a notice to disclose a phone PIN number to police.

"The charges follow an allegation made to police that damage had been caused to a boat in the Channel whilst an emergency responder was on board. He was remanded in custody to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates’ Court tomorrow (Friday 25 September)."

His arrest came after Thomas allegedly slashed a dinghy while a rescue worker was on board. The boat had previously carried some 50 migrants who left Normandy for the UK.

The migrants were picked up by RNLI crew after they reached the British search and rescue area. They were then transferred to a UK Border Force vessel and were later taken to Dover where they were processed.

Thomas filmed the transfer and gave commentary to the audience of some 15,000 viewers. The clip appeared to show him manoeuvring up close to the small boat before slashing it.

Several hundred people, largely wearing black, gathered outside a police investigation centre in Basingstoke this evening, believing that Thomas was inside.

They arrived together at just before 6.30pm and stood on the road outside the investigation centre and began chanting “free DT”. Most were not masked, though some could be seen wearing face coverings.

Dozens of police officers could be seen monitoring the group outside the investigation centre as the protest continued for several hours.

The demonstration was peaceful, with the group moving out of the road to make way for approaching traffic.

News.title: M61 traffic: Huge oil spill from HGV leaves southbound motorway closed in Greater Manchester
News.content:
There were delays on the M61 southbound in Greater Manchester (file image)

The M61 southbound in Greater Manchester was closed on Thursday after a lorry left a 'significant' oil spill across the carriageway

An oil spill stretching for around 2km has closed the M61 southbound in Greater Manchester, with motorists facing three miles of congestion and delays.

National Highways said two separate incidents took place on the M61 southbound on Thursday morning - a "significant" oil spill from an HGV and a car fire. It said the oil spill led to the closure of the carriageway between junction four (Watergate Lane Interchange), near Farnworth in Bolton, and junction two (Worsley Braided Interchange), near Worsley in Salford.

The HGV spilled oil across lanes one and two for around 2km (1.2 miles) as it travelled along the motorway at about 8.20am, National Highways said. The carriageway was closed to allow the spill to be cleared safely.

Separately, fire crews attended a car fire on the M61 southbound between junction five (Hunger Hill Interchange), near Westhoughton in Bolton, and junction four shortly after 9.30am, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said.

The vehicle was moved to the hard shoulder and crews remained at the scene for about 20 minutes. No injuries were reported.

News.title: Moment young boy is plucked out of the English Channel during small boat rescue
News.content:
Moment young boy is plucked out of the English Channel during small boat rescue

The video emerged on Thursday, the same day the Home Office confirmed 781 migrants arrived in Britain on Wednesday - beating the previous high so far this year of 752 on July 29

View 2 Images Video footage captured a man seemingly abandon a child before scrambling onto a dinghy in France (Image: NowherePhotographer)

Shocking images emerged today showing a child caught up in chaotic scenes in the English Channel - as it was announced 781 people reached Britain on small boats in a single day earlier this week.

‌



Video captured the boy, thought to be aged about three or four, being carried through waves by a man, who then appeared to abandon him face-up in the water while attempting to clamber up onto a dinghy. A member of the French lifeboat organisation, the SNSM, are seen seemingly attempting to pull the man back while plucking the the boy out of the water to safety and putting him on a surfboard.

‌



The clip was filmed near Berck beach, about 30 miles south of Boulogne, on Monday afternoon. It is not known if or how the man and child, who was dressed in a black, hooded anorak and an orange lifejacket, are connected.

‌



RNLI warned of cyber attack after volunteers abused for saving migrants by far-right thugs READ MORE :

View 2 Images The child was left floating in the sea for a few seconds, face up (Image: NowherePhotographer)

The video emerged on Thursday, the same day the Home Office confirmed 781 migrants arrived in Britain on Wednesday - beating the previous high so far this year of 752 on July 29. The figure is more than five times the average number seen on a normal 'red day' – when weather conditions and other factors make Channel crossings more likely.

Article continues below

And comes after two "uncontrolled landings" earlier this week when small migrant boats reached Kent without being intercepted by the authorities. Overall numbers remain significantly down compared to previous years.

A Home Office spokesman said: "Our progress this year in tackling small boats is indisputable – with crossings down by 42 per cent and the lowest recorded over the summer months since 2020. But this week's events show that while the peaks we are seeing are far below those of previous years, we need to push further and harder in order to eradicate this vile trade."

News.title: Partygoer dressed as Batman saves the day when he catches bag snatcher in the street
News.content:
Partygoer dressed as Batman saves the day when he catches bag snatcher in the street

Batman may usually patrol the streets of Gotham City, but one unlikely crime stopper brought a taste of superhero action to Norwich after a birthday celebration turn an unexpected turn

Real-life batman saves the day

A partygoer dressed as Batman turned into a real-life superhero when he chased down a handbag thief and helped reunite a woman with her stolen belongings.

‌



Sonni Mason, 25, had been celebrating a friend's birthday in Norwich on Saturday when he spotted a man snatching a woman's bag outside a bar on Queen Street. Still wearing his Batman costume, he sprang into action, chasing the suspect through the city centre before flagging down a police officer for help.

‌



But his superhero stint was far from finished. After tracking down the missing handbag, he had to claim a wall near Norwich Cathedral to recover it.

‌



Sister's heartbreak as Brit brother disappears abroad leaving family desperate for answers READ MORE :

Hero Brit saved others before he was killed by terrorist's rocket launcher at Mozambique beach hotel READ MORE :

View 4 Images Norwich has its own batman (Image: Joe Frankham / SWNS)

And despite being dressed as Gotham City's famous crimefighter, Sonni's homemade grappling hook, made from a recycled toilet roll, wasn't quite up to the job. Instead, he needed a boost from one of his friends to reach the bag.

Fortunately, his friends were suitably dressed for the occasion, with Mr Fantastic, Poison Ivy and Cyclops all joining Norwich’s own Batman.

‌



The ordeal began when a stranger joined Sonni and his friends as they queued outside a bar. Although he initially appeared friendly, the man allegedly accused two women of stealing his cigarettes before grabbing a handbag and fleeing. Sonni's quick thinking meant the bag was eventually recovered with everything still inside and returned to its owner.

View 4 Images Sonni Mason's quick thinking meant the bag was eventually recovered with everything still inside and returned to its owner. (Image: Joe Frankham / SWNS)

Speaking to the Eastern Daily Press, Sonni said: "There's not a lot of good things going on in the world. At the time, being able to get someone's bag back, [making] sure she could go home safe and see[ing] someone happy again felt good.

‌



"Everyone needs a little bit of that in them. A little bit of Batman. You have to be brave, bold and kind."

Footage of his unlikely crime-fighting adventure was shared on TikTok, where it has attracted more than 300,000 views.

Sonni regularly posts videos of himself dressed as superheroes, including Daredevil and Cyclops, but his latest outing gave him the chance to put his costume to a more practical use.

‌



View 4 Images Sonni describes himself as 'a bog-standard guy' (Image: Sonni Mason / SWNS)

Despite his heroic efforts, Sonni admitted his everyday life bears little resemblance to that of Batman's billionaire alter ego, Bruce Wayne. He works at a local café and has a passion for filmmaking.

He said: "I'm a bog-standard guy, to be honest, I currently work at a café, but I'm a creative at the core. I love films and have four or five years of experience in that industry."

‌



And while his costume might have inspired his actions, he explained he’s didn’t imagine the night would take the heroic turn. He said: "I didn't want to jump off rooftops or beat people up. I just want to make sure everyone else is all right. Sincerely, that's what [Batman] is about. He's a protector.

"I just hope more people will be inspired to do the same if they see someone being mugged or feeling uncomfortable on a night out."

View 4 Images The 25-year-old man hopes his actions will encourage others to look out for people on their night out (Image: Joe Frankham / SWNS)

Article continues below

Norfolk Police confirmed officers had been approached for assistance during their routine patrols on Saturday, September 19. No arrests were made.

A police spokesman said: "Officers on routine night-time economy patrols in Norwich were approached by a member of the public, on Saturday, September 19, who requested help to find a missing bag."

The spokesman added: "Following enquiries at the scene, the bag was located with all of its contents intact and subsequently returned to its owner."

News.title: Menu for Trump's dinner with Xi revealed as Melania prepares banquet for billionaires
News.content:
Menu for Trump's dinner with Xi revealed as Melania prepares banquet for billionaires

It is Chinese president Xi Jinping’s first visit to the US capital in more than a decade, and follows a state visit by Donald Trump to Beijing in May

View 3 Images President Donald Trump (R) stands with president Xi Jinping at the White House today (Image: Getty Images)

The menu for the dinner Donald Trump is hosting for Chinese premier Xi Jinping has been released.

‌



The sumptuous three course meal will be served up at a glitzy event at the White House with a star-studded guest list of tech and business leaders alongside political heavyweights.

‌



It is the Chinese president’s first visit to the US capital in more than a decade. At the top of the agenda are trade relations and the creation of an AI dialogue to discuss risks posed by the technology.

‌



Tonight’s official state dinner will see Trump and Xi joined by their wives along with a host of Big Tech and Wall Street executives.

View 3 Images China's First Lady Peng Liyuan, China's President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and US First Lady Melania Trump (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Tempers flare at Trump-Xi meeting as Chinese press clash with White House staff READ MORE :

On the guest list are Tesla boss Elon Musk, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, Jane Fraser from Citigroup and Apple’s former chief Tim Cook.

‌



First Lady Melania Trump, who oversaw preparations for the dinner, has included a nod to the guests’ homeland. Chinese flavours include a drizzle of scallion oil with the soup course and the sesame-seed crust on the Sea Bass main course.

President Xi hosted the US leader in May in a pomp-and-ceremony-filled state visit in Beijing, which included a dinner featuring Chinese dishes that are traditionally also popular in the US, including pork buns and Peking duck.

View 3 Images Presidents Trump and Xi and their wives look on during a military review in the Rose Garden of the White House (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



Full menu for Trump and Xi's dinner

First Course

Yellow Squash Velouté

Wild Mushroom Fricassée

Crispy Pancetta

Scallion Oil

Second Course

Sesame Crusted Sea Bass

Braised Baby Bok Choy

Roasted Garden Aubergine

Sauce Verte

Dessert

Vanilla Crémeux & White House Honey Ice Cream

Walnut Frangipane

Sour Cherry Confit

‌



Tensions flare as Trump meets Xi

While the diplomacy between the two leaders appears to have been smooth, things have been a little more turbulent behind the scenes during today's state visit.

Tempers appeared to flare between US officials and the visiting media with US special service officials seen pushing and shoving Chinese photographers moments before Donald Trump welcomed Xi Jinping to the White House.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Article continues below

Temperatures rose amid journalists jostling for position by the White House lawn, with a clip showing how US officials had to push Chinese media behind a barrier.

News.title: Boos and mass walkout for Netanyahu at UN as he rages at 'moral cowards'
News.content:
Boos and mass walkout for Netanyahu at UN as he rages at 'moral cowards'

Dozens of delegates at the UN General Assembly left the chamber as Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu took to the stage

View 2 Images Delegates walked out as Netanyahu took the stage (Image: Getty Images)

Dozens of delegates booed and walked out of the UN General Assembly as Benjamin Netanyahu took to the stage today.

‌



The Israeli leader lambasted those leaving the chamber before starting his speech, saying: “If there are any other moral cowards who haven't yet left this hall, please do so now."

‌



Small sections of the audience - including the Israeli delegation - could be seen applauding Netanyahu.

‌



It comes as he appears to have been snubbed by Donald Trump this week, as there are no plans for them to meet.

The snub hasn't stopped Netanyahu making a fiery speech. He boldly said "we'd all be dead" if Israel and the US didn't attack Iran earlier this year and devastate its "nuclear facilities".

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



Tempers flare at Trump-Xi meeting as Chinese press clash with White House staff READ MORE :

He also pointed to a speech he made 14 years ago on the same podium, during which he "drew a red line" and "vowed to prevent Iran's murderous dictatorship from developing atomic bombs".

Netanyahu claimed attacking Iran was one of the "easiest decisions I've ever had to make as prime minister".

Hitting out at those who left the room, he said Israel was defending many of their countries and accused them of "hypocrisy", saying many of their leaders "thanked us privately for taking out Iran's nukes".

‌



A defensive Netanyahu used his speech to deny his country has enacted a genocide on the Palestinians, branding the claims "the greatest lie of the century".

View 2 Images Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York following boos (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Netanyahu cited claims from a retired US army officer who said Israel has "done more to prevent civilian casualties in war than any other military in history".

‌



More than 69,000 people have been killed in Gaza, including 17,000 children, according to figures from the British Red Cross, with a further 170,000 people injured.

Netanyahu is currently the subject of an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court on November 21, 2024 for the alleged war crime of starvation as a method of warfare and the crimes against humanity of murder, persecution, and other inhumane acts during the Gaza war.

A UN-commissioned inquiry previously found Israel has committed genocide against Palestinians in war-torn Gaza.

‌



Netanyahu's brief visit also demonstrated how isolated he is globally, three years after launching a punishing war in Gaza in retaliation for the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023.

He faces re-election next month in polls widely seen as a referendum on his responsibility for the security failures surrounding the attacks and his ability to defend its reputation on the world stage.

Day after day this week, as other heads of state have stepped to the podium, many have harshly criticized Israel's actions, particularly in Gaza. Ahead of his visit, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani urged his arrest, saying the US should honour the ICC arrest warrant for Netanyahu. However the US is not a member of the court and New York City lacks the authority to arrest him.

Article continues below

Netanyahu's cold reception at the UN General Assembly is unlikely to faze him however, with his main audience the Israeli voters back home.

"He times his speech so that it is broadcast here in primetime," said Michael Oren, a former Israeli ambassador to the US who served under Netanyahu and lives in Israel.

News.title: Watch: Why has Trump been so eager to welcome Xi?
News.content:
US President Donald Trump has been talking for months about Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Washington DC. He's spruced up the White House, lamented that his new ballroom won't be finished in time and ensured a new marble helipad is ready to show off to the Chinese leader.

Trump gave Xi a warm welcome on his arrival at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, complete with a military flyover and a 100ft (30m) red carpet.

The BBC's North America Editor Sarah Smith explains how Trump has long made no secret of his admiration for strongman leaders around the world.

Follow the visit here.

News.title: Anti-migrant activist charged after dinghy slashed in Channel
News.content:
Anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has been charged with criminal damage after a video appeared to show him slashing at a dinghy in the English Channel.

The 37-year-old, known to his supporters as Danny Tommo, has also been charged with failing to disclose the PIN to his phone, Hampshire Police said.

He has been remanded in custody and is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court via videolink on Friday, the force added.

Several hundred people, many wearing black, had gathered outside a police investigation centre in Basingstoke on Thursday evening believing Thomas was inside.

The demonstration, which seemed to pass off peacefully, began shortly before 18:30 BST. Protesters stood on the road outside the building and could be heard chanting "free DT".

The crowd began to disperse at about 21:45 after they learned of the charges against Thomas.

Hampshire Police earlier said an arrest had been made after a "boat that had an emergency responder on board" was damaged in the Channel.

Thomas, of no fixed address, was held on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life, "destroying ships" under the Aviation and Maritime Security Act 1990 and "conduct endangering ships" under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.

The force previously said it was examining the video which had been live-streamed on Tuesday.

A French coastguard official was on board when Thomas appeared to slash at the vessel.

Some 50 migrants who had travelled in the boat from Normandy had already been transferred on to RNLI lifeboats. They were later moved on to a UK Border Force vessel and taken to Dover for processing.

News.title: Netanyahu defends Israeli military actions in Middle East in UN speech
News.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has fiercely defended his country's military campaigns in Iran, Gaza and elsewhere in the Middle East in a speech to the UN General Assembly.

After dozens of delegates walked out in protest as he took to the stage, Netanyahu vowed to continue fighting: "We're going to win. We have no other choice."

In response to the walkout, he said: "If there are any other moral cowards who haven't left the hall, please do so now."

The Israeli leader also rejected accusations that Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

Hours earlier, in a recorded message Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas told the UN that Israeli policies - in particular the illegal expansion of Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank - threatened "the very life and existence of the Palestinian people on their homeland".

He also said it jeopardised the two-state solution, which is an internationally backed formula for peace between Israel and the Palestinians.

Abbas said that Palestinians were being subjected to "killing, destruction, starvation and attempts at displacement, as well as a genocidal war" in Gaza by the Israeli military.

The Palestinian leader was addressing the annual gathering via a video link because had been denied a US entry visa.

News.title: Poland says fire at Starlink station is sabotage as Denmark warns of rising Russian threat
News.content:
A fire at a Starlink satellite station in central Poland was a deliberate "act of sabotage", a government minister has said.

Polish Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said the fire in the Masovian Voivodeship province was "deliberately designed to disable the station... disrupting internet access for various institutions, including the Ukrainian army".

He told Polish public broadcaster TVP Info an investigation was ongoing but "many indications suggest" the attack fits into a "new Russian doctrine of attack". The Kremlin has not commented.

Meanwhile, Denmark's intelligence service issued a new threat assessment saying it expects Russia to escalate hybrid warfare in the coming months.

It said an attack remained "highly unlikely" but warned of "a low but growing risk" that Russia could launch a limited military attack against Nato countries.

In recent weeks a number of European Nato members have said Russia may be preparing attacks to test their commitment to supporting Ukraine, which Moscow denies.

Earlier this month, Germany blamed Russia for an attempted drone attack on Leipzig/Halle Airport, while France has ordered a plan to protect critical infrastructure and defence industry sites.

Hybrid warfare or hybrid attacks are loose terms which tend to describe non-military methods designed to exert pressure and destabilise an adversary - for example cyberattacks, sabotage or misinformation.

Proxies are often used to carry out the attacks and Russia always denies involvement, despite growing evidence to the contrary.

News.title: Man jailed for two years over throwing bottle at Portsmouth migrant protest
News.content:
Judge Daniel Sawyer told Somerville that his sentence would act as a deterrent to others following subsequent protests in the area.

Describing him as a "thug", he told the defendant: "Police officers dedicate their lives to the protection of the public regardless of their own views, the very least they can expect is that those who engage in protests treat them with respect and the courts punish those who assault them."

The court heard Sommerville, from Portsmouth, was among a large group of demonstrators protesting at the arrival of the migrants.

They were brought ashore by the RNLI after being picked up in the Channel. A number of volunteer lifeboat crew members were subject to online abuse following the incident.

Prosecutor Edward Warren said Somerville was part of an "initially peaceful and lawful" gathering of a number of people on Ferry Road.

At shortly before 23:30 BST, he was with a large group of men as they were held up by the police line.

The court was told he was identified in police body-worn video as throwing a small bottle and swearing at police.

When later interviewed by police, he said he had found the bottle on the ground and was going to throw it into a nearby bush, but was angry and so threw it up into the air.

Defence barrister Helen Easterbrook said Somerville had been "caught up" in the disturbances.

She said he had been attempting to be a "calming influence" on the crowd but had thrown the bottle "in frustration".

Four other men are awaiting sentence having also been charged with violent disorder following the protest in Eastney.

News.title: 'We are living a constant nightmare,' mother of poison seller victim tells hearing
News.content:
The mother of a British victim of poison seller Kenneth Law has said his death and the way that he died had "destroyed" their family.

Tanya Whitaker broke down at the start of her video statement about the death of her son, Samuel, shown on the second day of a four-day sentencing hearing of Law in Ontario, saying: "He barely had a chance."

The University of Warwick student was found collapsed outside his halls after taking poison sold by Law, who has admitted 14 counts of aiding suicide in Canada. British authorities have confirmed 79 UK victims also died after using his products.

Debbie Cornish echoed Whitaker's sentiments, telling the hearing that her family was "still fighting" to stay together years on from her daughter Danielle's death.

A plea deal with Canadian authorities means Law will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths, but impact statements from their families are being read this week.

"The enormity of losing a child is catastrophic," Whitaker told a Canadian court on Thursday. "Samuel was just 19 when he was handed the tools that ended his precious life."

She continued: "It has broken me completely and utterly. It has broken us as a family and me as a mother.

"Our son died alone at university 100 miles away from his family. We will never be able to forgive ourselves for this happening."

News.title: Ex-England striker Andy Carroll reveals he was sexually assaulted in 2021
News.content:
Former England striker Andy Carroll has revealed he was sexually assaulted by a man in 2021.

The 37-year-old, who was automatically granted anonymity as a victim of sexual assault, has made the details public in an autobiography titled 'Owning it'.

The incident took place at Carroll's home, during his second spell with his hometown club Newcastle and led to the perpetrator being jailed for three years.

Carroll, now a player/co-owner of non-league club Dagenham & Redbridge, says he decided to include the incident in his book "at the very last minute" after discussing it with his girlfriend Lou Teasdale.

A friend of his former partner, who was away at the time, was set to stay over after coming to his home to watch a boxing match.

Carroll says the incident occurred while he was sleeping and he then threw the man out of the house, before knocking him unconscious as he tried to return.

Carroll, who also played in the Premier League for Liverpool and West Ham, called the police and was "sobbing" in the arms of his children's nanny.

The unnamed attacker was found guilty of sexual offences and placed on the sex offender register. Carroll testified in court, a process he says was "humiliating and embarrassing and absolutely horrendous".

Carroll wrote: "I was sexually assaulted, there I said it. Scary to even think about and only a few people knew about it before now.

"Me and Lou spent a lot of time discussing whether to mention it in this book or not. I avoided my publisher for so long that they probably suspected I got cold feet.

"Scary to talk about but it's made [me] the person I am today as much as any of the good stuff. And if me talking about it helps just one person then good, it will have been worth it."

Carroll, who won nine England caps, added: "What happened to me affected every facet of my life. I'd think about it every day, making it difficult to focus on anything else, including footballâ¦ The trauma of what happened to me hasn't gone away."

Carroll joined Dagenham in July 2025 and has made six appearances in the National League South this season.

If you have been affected by any of the issues in this article, you can find information and support at BBC Action Line

News.title: Crashed RAF jet steered to 'avoid built-up areas' before pilots ejected, commander says
News.content:
An RAF jet was steered to "avoid built-up areas" before two pilots ejected out of the aircraft, an air force commander has said.

Gp Capt Gez Currie, Station Commander, said: "The aircraft would have been aimed in a direction that the pilot believed was open field, in order to avoid built-up areas and anybody on the ground."

The Hawk T2 aircraft had been flying out of the RAF Valley station on Anglesey on Wednesday when it plummeted to the ground in nearby Pencarnisiog, narrowly avoiding homes.

The trainee and an experienced professional, who parachuted out of their plane moments before it crashed, are expected to make a full recovery after they were treated for minor injuries.

Hawk operations have been paused by the RAF as a "precautionary measure" while investigations into the crash are ongoing - the Red Arrows are included in the pause as the aerobatics display team use the T1.

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) confirmed that the squadron of Hawk jets at RAF Leeming, in Yorkshire, has also "paused" flying.

News.title: NHS trust to review 4,500 more breast cancer cases after failings
News.content:
Hospital chiefs in County Durham have agreed to review up to a further 4,500 breast cancer cases after failings including delayed diagnoses and unnecessary surgeries were found.

Hundreds of patients suffered harm under County Durham and Darlington NHS Foundation Trust, according to a review of cases dating back to 2023.

The BBC previously investigated the failings and has spoken to multiple women affected, including one who said she felt "mutilated" and the trust's mistakes were "absolutely unforgivable".

Ahead of agreeing to expand the review to cases dating back to 2015, members of the trust's board offered "sincere" apologies for the failings and harm caused.

At an extraordinary meeting of the board held in Durham, board chair Alison Marshall said: "I would like to offer a sincere apology to all the women and their families who have been affected by the failings in our breast services.

"I can't imagine the impact that has had."

She said they could "not turn back the clock" but would be "open, honest and transparent" about the failings.

Chief nurse Gill Hunt told the board concerns were first raised in 2015 after a "service reconfiguration" and loss of breast surgical trainee posts.

Over the following years patients and bodies such as the Northern Cancer Alliance, Care Quality Commission and NHS England raised multiple issues, she said.

The key "themes" included treatment "not aligned to best practice", excessive surgery and delayed diagnosis, she said.

The trust's breast surgery lookback review began in April 2025 by examining cases between January 2023 and February 2025.

Hunt said 538 cases had been reviewed so far with 321 having experienced some form of harm, including one death.

News.title: Sex offender bailed to flat near playground
News.content:
A sex offender jailed for taking thousands of pictures of children and using AI software to "nudify" them was repeatedly allowed to return to his home overlooking the playground he targeted.

It meant victims of Zafer Dogan, from Enfield in north London, were living close to the 32-year-old, who admitted multiple offences.

Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley spoke outside Wood Green Crown Court after Dogan was jailed for two years and four months, where Sir Mark criticised the "unfathomable decisions" of the justice system.

"The children should be put first, not the paedophile," he said.

News.title: Firm fined £1m after man killed by window that fell from luxury penthouse
News.content:
Ferris said her husband's death was "so sudden" and "out of the blue".

She said in a statement read out in court: "If somebody had done something differently â anything â it would have changed our lives. We wouldn't be in this position.

"I know it wasn't just one person, but one person could have changed this.

"What those companies did killed my husband.

"The thought this could have happened to anybody is always with me. It could have been a child."

She also told the court that 400 people attended her husband's funeral, and said "he is missed by so many it was unbelievable".

At the time of the incident, television host and fellow West Ham fan James Corden paid tribute to Mick Ferris on Twitter, saying: "He was a huge West Ham fan and has passed away in the most sudden of circumstances."

He added: "Tell your loved ones you love them today."

Health and Safety Executive principal inspector James Goldfinch said: "The fact lessons had not been learnt from a near miss the year before makes what happened on that day all the more galling.

"For a window to fall once was quite extraordinary, for it to fall again was simply criminal."
