Sports.title: Lawson blames F1’s rules for high closing speeds as stewards reprimand Hamilton | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Liam Lawson says Formula 1’s rules are to blame for the near-miss between him and Lewis Hamilton during practice in Baku.

The Racing Bulls driver caught Hamilton in the blind, flat-out turns 18 and 19 near the end of the lap.

The stewards reprimanded Hamilton for impeding his rival. However Lawson said the situation is a consequence of F1’s rules.

Drivers on a flying lap in Baku will use their battery energy to accelerate out of turn 16 through the flat-out corners to the point Lawson encountered Hamilton. But those not pushing to set a lap time will not do the same, creating a significant speed difference between the two.

“It’s just unfortunately the way the regs are that you have a situation like this,” said Lawson. “Obviously it’s quite sketchy when you’re the car approaching – either one of us, to be honest.”

Lawson predicted it will be difficult for drivers to avoid similar situation unless something is changed before tomorrow’s sessions.

“There’s not really a lot you can do,” he said. “When you look at it, Lewis comes out of 16 and he’s full throttle, he’s got two or three seconds to me, which is normally plenty of gap, but the speed difference is just so big.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“He’s not deploying anything. I’m deploying everything and so you have 60, 70, 80 kph speed difference, which is bad.

“The problem is, if he gets out of the way before 18 and slows down and then if there’s another car behind me, then the speed difference is enormous. So it’s something we have to look at overnight.

“If there’s something that we can do, it’s going to have to be before 16, honestly, because once you come out of that corner and you’re committed, there’s nothing honestly you can do. So it was just unfortunate.”

Race director Rui Marques has issued special guidelines for this weekend’s race instructing drivers to avoid impeding cars behind them after turn 16.

“Cars on out laps or slow laps should keep extreme left (i.e. not “offline” in middle of track) from exit [turn] 16 through to entry turn 18,” the rules state.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We consider that teams / drivers can and should manage traffic gaps before turn 18 (going as slowly as required being on the extreme left) to ensure that they can transit between the apex of turn 18 and apex of turn 19 without impeding an approaching car that is trying to set a competitive lap time.

“Cars on out laps or slow laps should keep ‘extreme’ right exit turn 19 until they achieve relevant speed to open the following lap.”

The stewards stated Hamilton failed to follow the guidance and issued him a reprimand.

“[Hamilton] was on an out-lap and [Lawson] was approaching on a flying lap,” they noted. “Hamilton had been informed twice by his team that Lawson was approaching.

“The Race Director’s Competition Notes require cars on out laps or slow laps to remain on the extreme left from the exit of turn 16 to the entry of turn 18, and require teams and drivers to manage their gaps before turn 18 so that they can travel from the apex of turn 18 to the apex of turn 19 without impeding a car on a competitive lap.

“Hamilton did not remain on the extreme left between Turns 16 and 18. Approaching turn 19, while Lawson was closing from behind, Hamilton stayed on the racing line which required Lawson to lift and slightly brake. The stewards therefore determined that Hamilton did not follow the traffic-management instructions and unnecessarily impeded Lawson.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The normal penalty for an impeding infringement during free practice is a warning unless it is dangerous or with intent. In this case, there was no intent but given the layout and the high speed corners as well as the specific instructions given by the race director, the impeding in the stewards’ opinion was severe.

“The stewards also took into account the difficulty to manage the energy deployment from turn 16 to turn 19 and the end of the lap. Additionally, both drivers mentioned during the hearing that when a driver has no more energy to deploy the difference of speed between the two cars in that specific section is important.

“Taking these circumstances into account, the stewards impose a driving reprimand.”

F1 altered its power unit rules earlier in the year to reduce the risk of high closing speeds causing a crash. This came after Oliver Bearman suffered a high-speed crash at Suzuka when he closed suddenly on Franco Colapinto’s Alpine.

Sports.title: Pictures: Chadwick tests Williams F1 car at Algarve circuit | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Williams’ ambassador Jamie Chadwick had her first test for the team at the Autodromo do Algarve in Portugal this week.

Chadwick completed 32 laps of the track on Monday.

“It was a phenomenal day and an incredible experience,” said Chadwick, who won the all-female W Series between 2019 and 2022.

“Few things can prepare you for driving a Formula 1 car at speed around a track like Portimao, but it was everything I imagined and 10 times more.”

Chadwick said she was “incredibly grateful” for the opportunity to drive the FW47, which the team raced last year.

“I remember being young and watching Susie Wolff step into a Williams F1 car and how much that inspired my own journey. I’d love to be able to do the same for the next generation, and the experience I gained today will make a real difference both to my own racing and to what I can pass on to the drivers coming through.”

Chadwick is the second woman to complete an F1 test this year. Mercedes junior Doriane Pin drove one of their cars in April.

The last woman to attempt to qualify for a grand prix was Giovanna Amati, in 1992.

Formula 1 will return to the Algarve circuit for the Portuguese Grand Prix next year.

Sports.title: Russell leads Mercedes one-two, Lindblad crashes, Hamilton summoned for impeding | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Mercedes were conclusively fastest in the second practice session for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Only one of the team’s rivals was able to get within a second of George Russell’s benchmark time. His best effort of 1’43.347 was also half a second faster than his team mate could manage.

Andrea Kimi Antonelli missed around half of the session as Mercedes completed the repairs to the championship leader’s car following the hydraulic problem which struck in first practice.

Max Verstappen was third-quickest for Red Bull but his quickest effort was over eight tenths of a second slower than Russell’s best. As usual, Verstappen was not happy with his car’s balance on the first day of practice, complaining the “rear axle is coming off the ground” early on.

Arvid Lindblad caused the session’s only red flag when he crashed at turn eight. The Racing Bulls driver damaged the right-hand side of his car and came to a stop.

His team mate Liam Lawson had a near-miss with Lewis Hamilton on the high-speed run through the final sector. “That is so fucking dangerous” complained Lawson after dodging Hamilton, who has been summoned to the stewards over the incident. Russell also had a close encounter with an Audi at the same point on the track, telling his team “I almost went straight into the back of Bortoleto.”

Once the session resumed, Russell easily beat Charles Leclerc’s time to go fastest, and remained there until the end. Lando Norris was on course to improve on his final run but he peeled off into the pits and ended the session in sixth place behind the Ferrari drivers.

Sports.title: Russell fastest as hydraulic problem halts Antonelli in first practice | Formula 1
Sports.content:
George Russell led the opening practice session for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix while a technical problem delayed his team mate.

Russell’s best lap, aided by a significant slipstream from a rival car, was exactly four-tenths of a second quicker than the next-closest driver, Max Verstappen. However Russell’s session almost came to an early end when he abandoned his attempt to take turn three and swerved into the run-off area, narrowly missing the barrier as he did.

Verstappen began the session strongly. The Red Bull driver was fastest over the opening 10 minutes, running on hard tyres, before Antonelli beat his time.

Despite his stoppage, the world championship leader ended the session with the fifth-fastest time. The two Ferrari drivers also beat him, Charles Leclerc only fractionally slower than Verstappen.

Liam Lawson returned to Racing Bulls after his brief stint at Red Bull’s senior team and set the sixth-fastest time. Isack Hadjar, back in the car Lawson drove in the last three races, was only able to do eight laps before Red Bull told him to stop due to a technical problem.

Nico Hulkenberg put his heavily updated Audi seventh-fastest. He briefly came to a stop near the end of the session but was able to resume.

Oscar Piastri set the eighth-fastest time with his final lap of the session. His running in McLaren’s updated MCL40 was disrupted when the team identified a potential problem on his team mate’s car and told him to stop, though Piastri was able to rejoin the track for a final lap.

Sports.title: Social Media: Ben Sulayem defends Gasly after latest abuse from Colapinto fans | Brief
Sports.content:
FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has condemned the online abuse directed at Pierre Gasly by supporters of his team mate.

Gasly briefly delayed Franco Colapinto during the latter stages of the Spanish Grand Prix two weeks ago. The driver and his family have since received abusive messages on social media.

“The online abuse directed at Pierre Gasly and his family is completely unacceptable,” said Ben Sulayem in a post. “Pierre has my full support, and I strongly condemn this behaviour. No driver, official, volunteer or fan should have to face this.

“Incidents like this are why I founded the United Against Online Abuse initiative. We simply cannot accept online hate within our sport and we all have a responsibility – governing bodies, teams, drivers, fans and social media platforms – to challenge this behaviour and create an environment built on respect.”

Colapinto’s supporters have been repeatedly accused of aiming abuse at drivers and other figures in the sport, including Jack Doohan last year, his own team this year and the FIA’s stewards last month.

“Competition and passion are at the heart of motorsport, but abuse has no place in it,” Ben Sulayem added. “We must continue to stand together and take meaningful action to protect everyone in our sporting community.”

Sports.title: Ocon confirms he is a “free agent” for 2027 as rumours link Camara to Haas | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Esteban Ocon looks set to leave Haas at the end of the season as the driver admitted he is a “free agent” for 2027.

The 30-year-old joined the team from Alpine last year. He was out-scored by rookie team mate Oliver Bearman last year and lies behind his team mate in the standings.

“At the moment I’m definitely a free agent for next year,” said Ocon in Baku. “[There are] all these discussions and there are certain topics in the background that are out of my control at this moment. Neither Haas driver has scored since Ocon’s ninth-place finish in Monaco.

“But I know that I’m exploiting the maximum of the package that I have every single time. So that’s strong.

Sports.title: Antonelli has “perfect driving style” for 2026 cars – Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is enjoying an extraordinarily successful second season in Formula 1 because his driving style works perfectly with the current generation of cars, says his team mate.

George Russell is Antonelli’s closest rival at the top of the championship standings, but the second-year driver is 81 points ahead. This is a sharp contrast to last year, when Russell out-scored Antonelli by 319 points to 150.

While Russell said Antonelli’s ability was clear before this season, he believes the reduction in aerodynamic downforce and grip this year has played to his team mate’s strengths.

“Of course Kimi is extremely talented,” said Russell. “He’s an incredible driver and has been fast in his whole career.

“I think his driving style is very similar to what he had last year and I think with just how things have fallen this year, it’s kind of the perfect driving style for these cars.”

Russell believes the same is true of other drivers, including Lando Norris, who is the only driver to have won more than one round this season.

“If you look last year, there are definitely trends,” said Russell. “If you look at Brazil last year, Kimi had a really strong race and Lando won in Brazil, and they’re two drivers who are always very strong on the low grip tracks and they’re two drivers who are arguably the best-performing drivers of this season.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“He’s an amazing driver and he was of course doing extremely well last year as well. Let’s see next year if it changes or not, but certainly his natural driving style suits very well for this regulation.”

Charles Leclerc echoed Russell’s view that Antonelli’s potential was clear despite his patchy rookie campaign last year.

“I wish I knew, but clearly he’s doing something that works very well,” said Leclerc. “But to be honest, it’s not that it comes as a complete surprise.

“If I look at Kimi going through the junior ranks, I think it was quite clear for everybody that he had something very special. If you look obviously at his first year in Formula 1, I think he probably faced challenges – it is not up to me to go into detail, I don’t know, but surely he had some struggles in the first year – but this year has been extremely impressive. I mean, from the first race to now, he’s been perfect and driving at a very high level against a driver that I rate extremely high as well, which is George. So he’s doing an incredible job.”

However Leclerc said there is only so much he can tell about Antonelli’s qualities from outside the Mercedes team.

“To [tell] you exactly why he’s so fast, and why he is outstandingly fast this year compared to last year, is very difficult for me. We are all here analysing the data of everybody but we can only go up to a certain amount of detail, then you really need the data of the actual car to dig into more detail.

“So it’s difficult. But his laps look a lot on the limit but somehow he manages to do the lap when it counts and that’s been very impressive to watch.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua Fight for WBA Super Title
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are receiving an unearned gift from the World Boxing Association. Neither Briton holds a world title, and their December 11 spectacle in Cardiff on Netflix certainly requires no manufactured hardware to pack a stadium. The sanctioning body is tossing its top heavyweight prize into the ring anyway, staging a brazen demotion of the actual titleholder standing in the wings.

Murat Gassiev did everything asked of him. He earned his position in the ring, collected his status after Oleksandr Usyk vacated, and defended his position by stopping Peter Kadiru in July. His reward is watching the WBA invent a higher tier out of thin air to accommodate two fighters who enter the ring with zero championship claims.

The super champion designation was created to honor unifications and dominant multi-belt reigns. Fury and Joshua possess none of that hardware today. Handing an elite designation to a pair of contenders coming off non-title bouts shreds the integrity of the rankings. The organization relies on discretionary clauses in its rulebook, but pulling bureaucratic rank to vault two big-name fighters past an active titlist exposes pure promotional favoritism.

Commercial convenience drives the maneuver. Attaching a world title to a global Netflix event allows the sanctioning body to secure maximum bout fees and purse percentages capped at five hundred thousand dollars total between both corners. That payday completely derails the campaign the organization spent years trumpeting, abandoning its pledge to eliminate duplicate titles and reduce every division to a single recognized champion.

Cardiff promises massive global exposure, but it leaves the division splintered. The victor will inevitably chase an immediate rematch, an undisputed bout, or walk away into retirement. Gassiev will find zero incentive from the winner to stage a dangerous, low-reward clash.

If the sanctioning body possesses any credibility, it must establish a mandatory deadline ordering the Cardiff winner to face Gassiev within six months. Without an enforceable consolidation order, the super title remains an arbitrary marketing prop manufactured to reward commercial power while the real champion stays shoved to the curb.

Throwing a manufactured Super title onto this Cardiff event is an outright insult to the sport. Neither Fury nor Joshua enters this fight carrying championship momentum. Both were thoroughly solved and dethroned by Oleksandr Usyk, and both have spent the latter stages of their careers surviving shaky outings against fringe opposition rather than beating top-tier contenders.

Inventing a world title specifically for them rewrites the entire definition of what a championship represents. The primary outrage sits squarely with the blatant demotion of Murat Gassiev. The sanctioning body spent years running a public relations victory lap, swearing to clean up its reputation by phasing out multiple champions and establishing one belt per weight class.

That promise evaporated the second Netflix and the Saudi backers dangled a massive live event. Gassiev took care of business in the ring against Pulev and Kadiru, only to be shoved down to secondary status. For the casual viewers tuning in on Netflix, the graphics package will do its job. The broadcast will flash world title belts across the screen, the commentary team will talk about legacy, and the mainstream audience will swallow the idea that the winner is the true king of the heavyweight division.

Hardcore fans know better. A real world title cannot be handed out as a promotional party favor to two aging fighters years past their absolute prime. It degrades the division, reduces the belt to a rented stage prop, and reminds anyone paying close attention that in the heavyweight hierarchy, money and broadcast leverage will always trump genuine athletic merit.

Casual fans will view it as a real world title fight because the television screen tells them to. The mainstream audience does not follow sanctioning body mandates, title unifications, or mandatory rankings. They see two names they recognize from mainstream headlines, a stadium packed with seventy thousand screaming fans. To someone who watches boxing once every two years, whoever walks out of Cardiff with that belt looks like the king.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs  Anthony Joshua Finally Official: December 11 in Cardiff on Netflix
Sports.content:
The British heavyweight rivals will meet at Principality Stadium after a dispute over the venue delayed their long-awaited fight.

Tyson Fury (36-2-1, 25 KOs) and Anthony Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) will finally fight on Friday, December 11, 2026, at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, live on Netflix. The confirmation ends months of negotiations over where the British heavyweight clash would take place.

The venue dispute is settled. Joshua’s camp had insisted on staging the bout in Britain, while New York’s Madison Square Garden became a serious alternative.

“I can now confirm that Fury Vs Joshua will be coming to the UK, as I promised British boxing fans. The time for talking is over……..” Turki Alalshikh wrote on X.

Both fighters signed earlier this year. A date and venue remained unresolved, however, allowing the dispute to drag on despite their agreement to face each other. Fury repeatedly blamed Joshua in public and suggested he could pursue a third fight against Oleksandr Usyk.

Dana White said: “For more than a decade, boxing fans have been clamoring for the heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua. Together, they bring 66 wins, 52 knockouts and multiple heavyweight world titles into the ring. On December 11, two of the biggest heavyweights of this generation finally collide and the winner will take a significant place in heavyweight history.”

Netflix says White and The Ring will collaborate to promote the fight, despite Eddie Hearn’s earlier insistence that White would not be its promoter.

Joshua has boxed at Principality Stadium twice before, stopping Carlos Takam and then outpointing Joseph Parker to add the WBO heavyweight belt to his collection. He returns to face the British rival whose name has followed him through years of callouts and failed negotiations.

Both men came through summer bouts.

Joshua survived two first-round knockdowns against Kristian Prenga in July before stopping him in the second. Fury stopped Mariusz Wach after seven rounds in Thailand that month, having returned in April to outpoint Aslanbek Makhmudov at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Those victories kept their meeting alive. Now the former heavyweight champions have a confirmed December date in Britain, with Netflix carrying the broadcast.

Sports.title: Manny Pacquiao and Shakur Stevenson Remain in Cardiff Talks
Sports.content:
Manny Pacquiao against Shakur Stevenson remains under discussion for the proposed Anthony Joshua-Tyson Fury card in Cardiff. It would give the event a second major fight, but neither Pacquiao nor Stevenson has received a bout agreement.

BoxingScene’s Lance Pugmire reports that two people connected to the talks say Netflix wants the matchup as part of a “double main event.” December 11 is the date under consideration at Principality Stadium, with December 18 also possible. Pacquiao adviser Jas Mathur told BoxingScene that Pacquiao’s financial terms are still being negotiated.

That leaves a great deal to settle before anyone can call this a fight. The Cardiff show itself has yet to be formally announced, and moving Joshua-Fury from the previously discussed Madison Square Garden setting means assembling the rest of the card around a different venue and date.

Pacquiao-Stevenson would bring two very different attractions to that card. Stevenson, 29, is coming off his January win over Teofimo Lopez and has since signed with Zuffa Boxing. Pacquiao, 47, drew with Mario Barrios in his July 2025 return. His name would draw attention far beyond the usual boxing audience, though the long layoff and age difference would become part of the conversation as soon as the fight was announced.

The proposed pairing also raises a practical question: what weight would they fight at? Pacquiao’s return came at welterweight, while Stevenson’s recent work has been at lighter weights. No weight, number of rounds, or title terms have been announced.

For now, the news is that Pacquiao-Stevenson has survived the reported switch to Cardiff and remains in Netflix’s plans, according to BoxingScene. The decisive development would be agreements reaching both fighters. Until then, it belongs on the list of fights being negotiated, rather than the Joshua-Fury undercard.

Pacquiao turns 48 on December 17. If the fight lands on December 18, Shakur would face him one day after his birthday. Pacquiao won his first world title in 1998, before Shakur turned two.

That age difference makes the matchup a hard sell as a competitive fight. If Shakur wins easily, how much credit does he get for beating a man nearly two decades older? If he boxes his way to a quiet decision, Pacquiao’s name may bring viewers to Netflix, but the fight may give them little reason to watch Shakur again.

Pacquiao’s fame can make this a major event. Turning it into a fight that helps Shakur is another matter. First, both men need to agree to terms; neither has received a bout agreement.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Picks Leonard, But Ray Robinson Set The Harder Standard
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson prefers Sugar Ray Leonard to Sugar Ray Robinson. It is easy to see why. Leonard’s speed, movement, and command of distance resemble the qualities Shakur prizes in his own boxing. But Leonard’s finest wins also required him to fight through danger, and Robinson did that across a schedule neither man came close to matching.

“I like SRL better then I like SRR, This might make my people mad but SRL was one hellavu fighter to me his level was extremely high!!” said Shakur on X.

Stevenson posted that on X on September 22. He had previously called Robinson “buns,” then conceded Robinson was a great fighter and said he had been talking trash. His preference for Leonard is consistent with that view.

Leonard was no fighter who simply ran from trouble. He lost a hard 15 rounds to Roberto Durán, came back to beat him, and stopped Thomas Hearns late in their first fight. His footwork gave him choices; when those fights demanded more, he had offense and resolve to draw upon.

Robinson’s record makes the comparison tougher for Shakur. At age 29, Robinson was 108-1-2 with 72 knockouts. Shakur Stevenson (25-0, 11 KOs) has fought 25 times at the same age. Leonard had fought 34. Different eras produced different schedules, but Robinson’s total still speaks to his ability to win, recover, and do it again.

Shakur’s defense is exceptional. What remains unproven is how he would respond if his legs slowed and an opponent forced him to fight for long stretches at close range. Leonard showed he had answers when movement was insufficient. Robinson showed them more than a hundred times before his 29th birthday, backed by power Shakur has yet to display.

Shakur can like Leonard better. If he is judging the full range of what a fighter had to survive and deliver, Robinson deserves a closer look.

Nobody from modern eras, Leonard included, touches what Robinson accomplished by 29.

Robinson was 128-1-2 with 84 knockouts by the time he hit his 30th birthday, and that lone defeat to Jake LaMotta was avenged multiple times over. He was fighting every few weeks, traveling by car or train, taking on rugged contenders in 15-round fights with small gloves and no modern sports science. If Leonard had tried to keep that exact pace against that level of weekly attrition, his body would have broken down even sooner. Leonard had brittle hands and a detached retina by fight 28. Robinson had a jaw made of granite, brutal endurance, and lethal power in both hands.

Shakur picking Leonard makes sense purely through the lens of modern comfort. Leonard represents the blueprint Shakur relates to: the flashy television superstar, the Olympic gold medalist, the master of lateral movement, hand speed, and distance management. Leonard showed that a fighter could dictate terms, generate huge paydays, and maintain an aura without having to fight forty times a year in smoke-filled arenas.

Where Shakur’s comparison falls completely flat is what Leonard actually did when boxing finesse failed. When Leonard got pulled into absolute hell against Roberto Duran in Montreal, he stood flat-footed and fought. When he was fading and behind on the cards against Thomas Hearns, he unleashed a vicious, predatory assault to close the show. Leonard had a ruthless finishing instinct.

Shakur takes the defensive, perimeter-oriented parts of Leonard’s style and strips away the violent bite. Robinson was a destructive puncher who could knock an opponent out going backward or forward. Shakur is a pure points collector who treats contact like a disaster.

Shakur looking at Robinson and favoring Leonard sounds like modern revisionism. It is a fighter who relies on safety and low output, trying to validate his own approach, overlooking the fact that both Sugar Rays had an appetite for destruction that Shakur has never shown inside a ring.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia May Vacate Rather Than Fight Bektemir Melikuziev
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia may give up his WBA super middleweight title rather than defend it against Bektemir Melikuziev. Rick Glaser says Munguia’s team is considering that option. If his information is right, the decision would fit a career that has generally been managed with care. I expected Munguia’s team to have little appetite for Bek once the mandatory fight was ordered.

Glaser says Munguia’s camp is taking a “deep dive into the idea of giving up the title.” He has not said Munguia has vacated. The WBA has given the two sides until October 21 to make a deal and may call a purse bid if they fail to agree.

The Golden Boy connection makes this especially revealing. Melikuziev has fought under its banner since turning professional, and the company knows what its own fighter would bring against Munguia. Bek is a powerful southpaw with a damaging body attack. Munguia’s willingness to take punches while pressing forward would give him chances to land, but it would also give Bek chances to hurt him.

Munguia (46-2, 35 KOs) accepted the Canelo Alvarez fight for a huge payday and lost. Bruno Surace then knocked him out in a matchup Munguia was favored to win. Sergiy Derevyanchenko gave Munguia a hard fight, so his record is not free of risk. Melikuziev presents a different calculation: considerable danger with nowhere near Canelo’s commercial reward.

The WBA belt helped Munguia regain world champion status when he beat José Armando Reséndiz in May. Defending it is another matter. A purse bid could also take the choice of date, venue, and broadcaster out of his team’s hands. Vacating would leave Munguia free to pursue a bigger name at 168, though that freedom would come at Bek’s expense.

Melikuziev (17-1, 11 KOs) beat Darius Fulghum in a WBA eliminator in May 2025, then watched Munguia get the fight with Reséndiz. Bek told The Ring he had been assured he would get the next shot. If Munguia vacates, Bek may still get a chance to win the belt. He would lose the chance to win it from Munguia, a victory that would mean far more for his career.

We’re seeing the new age of belt-holders. Champions giving up their belts exposes the entire modern hustle around world titles. Fighters treat sanctioning body belts like disposable leverage tools rather than something to defend against legitimate threats. They want the belt purely to slap “world champion” on a poster, collect the promotional bump, and leverage it into an in-house payday.

The second a dangerous, low-profile puncher gets ordered as a mandatory, they drop the trinket in the trash and run. Look at the pattern playing out right now. Hamzah Sheeraz walked away from his belt rather than get in the ring with Janibek Alimkhanuly. Teofimo Lopez is on the verge of playing the same game,

Now Jaime Munguia’s camp looks ready to dump the WBA strap because Bektemir Melikuziev offers pure risk with zero casual crossover appeal. Bektemir is a nightmare matchup for a flawed fighter like Munguia. Bek is a heavy-handed, compact southpaw who specializes in cracking the ribs and punishing guys who march forward without defense.

Against Bektemir, Munguia risks getting stopped on regular DAZN for modest money, completely torpedoing his marketability for another mega-fight. Dumping the title completely strips away the pretense of championship prestige. Decades ago, winning a belt meant you took on whoever climbed the ladder, regardless of style or reward. What we’re seeing now is champions treating mandatory defenses like bad business propositions.

If Munguia vacates, Bektemir Melikuziev should get the first chance at the vacant WBA title, but the WBA would still have to choose his opponent. Its current rankings put Canelo Alvarez at No. 2 and José Armando Reséndiz at No. 3. A Canelo fight would be the biggest prize for Bek, though there is no indication Canelo wants it.

Reséndiz looks like the more realistic choice: he lost the belt to Munguia in May and would have a chance to win it back. That would give Bek a title opportunity, but it would deny him the higher-profile victory over Munguia that he has spent more than a year pursuing.

Sports.title: Cuban Boxing Greatness Crossed a Dividing Line
Sports.content:
Cuba produced professional stars before it became an Olympic boxing power. That history makes any list of its greatest fighters difficult to rank. Kid Chocolate and Kid Gavilan built their names in long professional careers; Teófilo Stevenson and Félix Savón never fought professionally. The dividing line was a political decision in 1962 that changed what a Cuban boxer could do with his talent.

Chocolate was a major New York attraction in the 1930s, admired for his speed and two-handed punching. Gavilan later won the welterweight title and made the bolo punch his signature. Luis Rodriguez added another championship to Cuba’s professional history when he beat Emile Griffith for the welterweight title in 1963. These men built their reputations in fights against the leading professionals of their day.

After Cuba banned professional boxing, a fighter who wanted that career had to pursue it abroad. José Nápoles became a welterweight champion after making his home in Mexico. José Legrá won the featherweight title while based in Spain. Later fighters such as Erislandy Lara left Cuba to compete for professional titles. Their success carried a personal cost that a list of wins and belts cannot show.

Cuba also built an amateur program under coach Alcides Sagarra that produced generations of Olympic champions. Stevenson won heavyweight gold in 1972, 1976 and 1980. Savón won the same prize in 1992, 1996 and 2000. Their medals need no imagined professional careers to give them value. But the absence of professional fights leaves one question open: how would the system’s best have performed against established champions over twelve rounds?

Guillermo Rigondeaux gave that question a partial answer. He won Olympic gold in 2000 and 2004, then left Cuba and became a professional champion. In 2013, he beat Nonito Donaire in a super bantamweight title fight, controlling distance and making a dangerous puncher miss repeatedly. Donaire was a proven champion, and Rigondeaux’s amateur schooling held up against him. One fight cannot settle how Stevenson or Savón would have fared as professionals, but it gives this comparison something firmer than speculation.

Lara’s December 2025 defense of the WBA middleweight title shows that Cuban fighters still succeed on the professional side of that divide. The strongest case for Cuba’s boxing greatness comes from looking at both sides: champions who proved themselves over long professional careers, Olympic greats whose careers took another course, and Rigondeaux, who crossed between them and beat one of the best.

Sports.title: Ben Whittaker Faces Conor Wallace With Little Buzz
Sports.content:
Matchroom’s countdown poster for the October 3 fight puts Ben Whittaker front and center in gold gloves, treating Conor Wallace like an afterthought tucked near the bottom. That tells you everything about how this IBF final eliminator is being sold. Matchroom wants the spectacle, yet they are hiding the very man brought in to provide a test at Birmingham’s Utilita Arena on DAZN.

The sanctioning body slapped a number two ranking on Wallace, dangling a mandatory shot at Dmitry Bivol for the victor. Matchroom calls this Whittaker’s most demanding fight to date, yet their own promotional material treats Wallace like a ghost.

Wallace is a heavy-handed southpaw who thrives on forward pressure, precisely the style that gave Whittaker fits against Liam Cameron. Cameron refused to play along with the showboating, got right in Whittaker’s chest, took away his operating room, and forced a difficult inside brawl that ended in a bizarre technical draw. That fight exposed the cracks in Whittaker’s viral persona.

Whittaker loves dropping his hands, leaning back, and relying on pure reflexes against timid opposition. A southpaw stepping outside the lead foot and drilling straight left hands down the pipe shatters that rhythm instantly. If Wallace gets past the jab, cuts off the ring, and forces Whittaker into the ropes, the fancy footwork disappears, leaving a grueling night of trench warfare.

Wallace built that top ranking touring the regional Australian circuit, highlighted by a narrow split decision win over Jerome Pampellone. Whittaker, despite his Olympic silver medal pedigree, spent his recent dates clowning against Richard Rivera, Braian Nahuel Suarez, and Benjamin Gavazi. Both fighters avoided the domestic shark tank of Joshua Buatsi, Willy Hutchinson, or Anthony Yarde to land in this position.

Taking an open sanctioning door is standard boxing business, but Dmitry Bivol waits on the other side. Bivol dismantles loose showmen with relentless robotic fundamentals, punishing anyone who drops their hands. Wallace is the final chance to discover if Whittaker has actual substance when an opponent fires back with bad intentions, and Matchroom is foolish to hide the danger.

Eddie Hearn labels Ben Whittaker a generational talent, but Matchroom matches him like an unpolished novice they are terrified of getting touched. If a promoter genuinely believes an Olympic silver medalist is that caliber of fighter, you do not keep him in bubble wrap for four years. Look at genuine generational fighters or top-tier Olympians: Vasiliy Lomachenko was fighting for a world title in his second professional bout. Sugar Ray Leonard, Floyd Mayweather Jr., and Andre Ward were dismantling legitimate, battle-tested contenders by their thirteenth fight.

Whittaker is 29 years old. He is not a 20-year-old kid who needs physical maturation or time to grow into his man strength. At his age, an elite fighter should be in his prime, yet Matchroom is treating this October 3 date with Conor Wallace like a massive hurdle rather than what it actually is: an exercise in matchmaking self-preservation.

Wallace is an eight-year pro whose record looks manufactured in a lab. He racked up wins on the Australian circuit against obscure opposition, barely edged Jerome Pampellone by split decision, and somehow landed the IBF number two ranking because the sanctioning bodies operate on regional belt accumulation rather than quality. S

erious boxing fans know Wallace is not a top ten light heavyweight in the world. He is a convenient mark with an inflated ranking.The fact that Matchroom selected Wallace for an IBF final eliminator instead of testing Whittaker against domestic threats tells the whole story. Why hasn’t Whittaker been matched against Joshua Buatsi, Anthony Yarde, Willy Hutchinson, or Dan Azeez? Those are the domestic names that would force Whittaker to prove he belongs.

Matchroom deliberately avoided that gauntlet because they know what happens when someone refuses to buy into the showmanship. The Liam Cameron fight gave away the game. When Cameron got inside, roughed Whittaker up, and took away his operating space, the flashy reflex defense fell apart. Whittaker looked ordinary, rattled, and completely out of ideas before that bizarre ring fall ended things in a technical draw. That reveals what Hearn and his team likely see behind closed doors in sparring. If a fighter looks unbeatable in the gym against world-class work, a promoter moves him fast to cash in.

When a promoter slow walks a 29-year-old Olympic medalist against handpicked opposition, it means the gym reports are raising red flags: leaks in the defensive fundamentals, getting clipped when trading on the inside, or an engine that cannot handle a relentless twelve-round pace.

It appears that Matchroom is trying to sneak Whittaker through an open back door to a massive payday against Dmitry Bivol without having him run a real gauntlet. Wallace was brought in to provide the illusion of a world-level eliminator without the actual danger. If Whittaker were the transcendent force Hearn claims, the training wheels would have come off years ago.

Sports.title: Gerrie Coetzee’s Bionic Hand Ends Michael Dokes’s Reign
Sports.content:
Michael Dokes had the faster hands and a title defense close to home on September 23, 1983. Gerrie Coetzee had two failed title bids and a reputation for fading late. Ten rounds later, Dokes was on the canvas, and Coetzee was the WBA heavyweight champion.

Don King billed the fight at Richfield Coliseum as “The Buckeye Homecoming,” though the crowd was about 7,000 in an arena that held 22,000. Dokes (26-0-2, 15 KOs), from nearby Akron, was a 5-1 favorite over Coetzee (28-3-1, 17 KOs). His title reign had begun with a disputed first-round stoppage of Mike Weaver, followed by a draw in their rematch.

Coetzee knew how a strong start could go wrong. John Tate had outlasted him over 15 rounds, and Weaver had stopped him in the 13th. Dokes showed his speed early and cut the challenger near the right eye in round two. Coetzee took the punches and kept coming.

His rebuilt right hand had earned him the nickname “The Bionic Hand,” and it remained one of his best weapons. Dokes had another punch to consider that night, though: Coetzee used his left hook more often than he had in earlier title bids. The hook made his attack less predictable while he pressed the quicker champion.

In the fifth, a short left-right combination put Dokes down on one knee. He rose quickly and fought back, but the knockdown changed the terms of the fight. Coetzee did not slow down as he had against Tate and Weaver. He stayed close enough to make Dokes work and reached the tenth ahead on all three official cards. Dokes still had good moments, particularly in the eighth; this was no uncontested march to the finish.

Coetzee landed two heavy rights past the midpoint of the tenth and followed Dokes into a corner. Dokes tied him up, but after referee Tony Perez separated them, Coetzee attacked again. A left-right combination sent Dokes down. The bell rang during the count, and Perez counted him out at the official time of 3:08.

The right hand helped Coetzee win the title on his third attempt. It also broke again, requiring surgery and keeping him out of the ring for more than a year. He lost the belt to Greg Page in his first defense. Dokes later admitted that cocaine and Jack Daniel’s had been part of his preparation, but that admission does not account for Coetzee’s work over ten rounds. On a night built to celebrate Dokes, the fighter everyone thought would fade was still throwing with force at the end.

Ghana News.title: AFCON 2027Q: Black Stars open campaign with defeat to Ivory Coast in Bouaké
Ghana News.content:
Ghana's hopes of making a winning start to their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign suffered a setback as the Black Stars lost 2-0 to Ivory Coast in Bouaké

Malick Yalcouye opened the scoring with a powerful strike from outside the box before Frank Kessie doubled the hosts' advantage from the penalty spot in the second half.

The defeat leaves Ghana at the bottom of Group C ahead of Friday's meeting between The Gambia and Somalia.

Ghana came into the game looking to return to the continental showpiece after missing the previous Africa Cup of Nations for the first time in 20 years.

However, Carlos Queiroz's side struggled to create clear opportunities against an Ivory Coast team that controlled much of the match.

The Black Stars were without several key players because of injuries, including captain Jordan Ayew, Manchester City winger Antoine Semenyo, Tottenham Hotspur forward Mohammed Kudus and Thomas Partey.

Brandon Thomas was tasked with leading the attack, with Christopher Bonsu Baah and Fatawu Issahaku operating alongside him and Ernest Nuamah playing behind the centre-forward.

Ghana created little during the opening stages, although Nuamah came close to giving the visitors a breakthrough midway through the first half.

The forward noticed the Ivory Coast goalkeeper off his line and attempted a long-range effort in the 20th minute, but his shot drifted wide.

The hosts eventually broke the deadlock in the 29th minute as Yalcouye produced a powerful effort from just outside the box into the bottom-right corner.

The scorer attacked down the left side of the penalty area and went to ground following a challenge from Fatawu.

The referee pointed to the spot, with Ghanaian players protesting the decision. After a lengthy delay, Kessie stepped up and converted from 12 yards in the 56th minute.

By that stage, Ghana had still failed to register a shot on target and had conceded 62% of possession to their opponents.

Queiroz responded with a triple substitution in the 64th minute.

Felix Afena-Gyan, Benjamin Tetteh and Augustine Boakye were introduced, replacing Nuamah, Brandon Asante and Christopher Bonsu Baah.

The changes brought some attacking urgency from Ghana, but the Black Stars were unable to find a way back into the contest.

It took until nearly the 80th minute for Ghana to register their first efforts on target, with Benjamin Tetteh and Caleb Yirenkyi testing the Ivory Coast defence.

Afena-Gyan and Augustine Boakye, who was making his long-awaited Black Stars debut, came close to reducing the deficit in stoppage time.

Ghana will now regroup as they look ahead to their next Group C fixture against The Gambia at the Accra Sports Stadium on September 29.

Ghana News.title: From construction site to top of class: Daniel Doe emerges Legon’s best Computer Engineering student
Ghana News.content:
Daniel Agudey Doe

Daniel Agudey Doe, a Computer Engineering graduate of the University of Ghana, has emerged as the best graduating student in his programme after navigating significant financial difficulties during his university education.

Before receiving financial assistance through the MTN Ghana Bright Scholarship, Daniel worked on construction sites and took on other manual labour jobs during vacations to raise money for tuition and living expenses.

His financial challenges also affected his ability to meet basic needs on campus, with occasions when he had to skip meals.

“I was simply trying to make it through university. If things became impossible and I had to drop out, at least I could say I had given university my best attempt,” he said.

Daniel entered the University of Ghana with an interest in Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning and hoped to eventually build a career in Robotics.

However, the financial demands of university meant that completing his degree was uncertain.

Scholarship eased financial pressure

That changed after he was selected as a beneficiary of the MTN Ghana Bright Scholarship.

The scholarship covered his tuition and hostel fees and provided additional support for his studies.

Daniel said the assistance allowed him to devote more attention to his academic work without having to spend his vacations primarily looking for money to return to school.

“For the first time, I had the privilege many financially stable students have, the ability to focus on my studies without constantly worrying about tuition, hostel fees, or survival,” he said.

With the financial pressure reduced, Daniel said he was able to participate more actively in group studies and devote more time to his coursework.

He eventually graduated as the Best Graduating Computer Engineering Student at the University of Ghana.

Daniel believes the financial support was critical to his completing the programme.

“Without the scholarship, I genuinely do not believe I would have completed university. I may have dropped out as early as Level 200 due to financial pressure,” he said.

From construction to technology

Daniel is currently undertaking his National Service at Amalitech as a Data Engineer.

He intends to build experience in data engineering before moving into Machine Learning and, eventually, Robotics.

He is also considering pursuing a master’s degree in Robotics or a related field combining Robotics and Artificial Intelligence.

Daniel said guidance from his scholarship coordinator, Mr George, also helped him consider his options ahead of his National Service placement.

Scholarship programme

Daniel is among students supported under the MTN Ghana Foundation’s Bright Scholarship programme, which was introduced in 2017.

According to information provided by the foundation, the programme has supported 1,220 students in tertiary institutions across Ghana.

The scholarship covers tuition and accommodation and includes support for a laptop, books and study materials.

The programme has also recorded several academic distinctions among its beneficiaries, with 17 scholars graduating as valedictorians or best students at their institutions and 299 graduating with first-class honours.

For Daniel, his journey from working on construction sites to graduating at the top of his Computer Engineering class demonstrates the difference financial support can make for students facing difficulties in funding their education.

“The MTN Bright Scholarship did not just change my life; it positively impacted my family and my community,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Mahama: Peaceful political transitions prove democracy can work in Africa
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama has pointed to Ghana’s record of peaceful political transitions as evidence that democratic institutions can provide a stable framework for managing changes in political leadership.

Addressing world leaders at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York, President Mahama said Ghana had remained committed to constitutional democracy, the rule of law and respect for human rights.

“Ghana is arguably the most stable democracy in Africa,” he said, adding that the country was determined to demonstrate that “democracy works”.

President Mahama said Ghana’s democratic system allows political differences to be resolved through constitutional processes, participation and consensus rather than through force or instability.

He acknowledged that democratic systems can sometimes be slower in taking decisions because they require consultation and adherence to constitutional procedures. However, he said those processes help create decisions that are more sustainable because they are rooted in participation and legitimacy.

The President said Ghana’s experience was also relevant to the broader African debate on democratic governance, particularly the need for political systems to deliver meaningful improvements in citizens’ lives.

He maintained that democracy should ultimately produce tangible social and economic benefits, including access to education, healthcare, housing, food and economic opportunity, alongside the protection of political and civil rights.

Ghana News.title: “The law must work” – NDC rejects claims Salomey Baffoe’s bail denial is diversion from cocaine scandal
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Director of Elections and IT for the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Rashid Tanko Computer, has rejected claims that the continued detention of Salomey Awiti Baffoe is a government strategy to divert public attention from the ongoing narcotics trafficking concerns.

He said the case must be allowed to follow due process, insisting that the government would not interfere with the work of the judiciary or security agencies.

Speaking on JoyFM’s Top Story on Thursday, September 24, Mr Tanko Computer said attempts to link the case to the cocaine controversy were, in his view, an attempt to avoid accountability under the law.

“You see, they rather want to divert attention by trying to run away from the law. The law is the law. They want to run away from the law,” he said.

His comments followed claims by Second Deputy Minority Whip and Weija-Gbawe MP Jerry Ahmed Shaib that the continued detention of Ms Baffoe was a “facade” intended to divert public attention from the narcotics trafficking cases.

Read also: Salomey Baffoe detention is a facade to divert attention from chttps://www.myjoyonline.com/salomey-baffoe-detention-is-a-facade-to-divert-attention-from-cocaine-scandal-weija-gbawe-mp/ocaine scandal – Weija-Gbawe MP

The High Court on Thursday denied a bail application filed on behalf of Ms Baffoe after the prosecution argued that she was still needed to assist with ongoing investigations.

The court said the investigation was cyber-related and that releasing the accused at that stage presented a real risk of interference with witnesses. It subsequently directed the Republic to expedite its investigations.

Mr Tanko Computer said the NDC would not support any attempt to undermine the work of state institutions in the name of political controversy.

“We won’t say because of these things that they are doing, we should fold our arms and allow them to allow the country to descend into an abyss. We won’t allow it,” he said.

He insisted that the government would allow the relevant institutions to carry out their responsibilities without political interference.

“And then the law, it must work. We will not allow anybody to interfere in the execution of the law. And that is what the government will not do,” he said.

Mr Tanko Computer also defended the NDC government’s position on judicial independence, saying the party would not interfere in the work of the courts.

“The NDC, we will not interfere in the judiciary. Look, we are noted for not interfering in the judiciary, unlike their time,” he said.

“The NDC under the watch of His Excellency John Dramani Mahama will not interfere in the judiciary when they are carrying out their exercise. We won’t do it,” he added.

He further called for security agencies to be allowed to conduct their investigations, warning that persons invited to assist with investigations could be pursued if they fail to cooperate.

“And then the security agents must be allowed to do their work. We can’t interfere in whatever they are doing. If you are invited to come and answer questions and you are running away from the law, you expect them to leave you. They will hunt you down,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Police arrest two suspects over murder of Senegalese goalkeeper
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Police Service has arrested two suspects in connection with the kidnapping and murder of Senegalese goalkeeper Cheikh Toure in Kumasi in October 2025.

The arrests followed a sustained intelligence-led operation by the Police to identify and apprehend persons linked to the death of the goalkeeper.

According to the Police, on October 16, 2025, some individuals who claimed to be brothers of the deceased took him to the Manhyia Hospital in Kumasi with multiple abdominal injuries.

The individuals told the hospital that the victim had been involved in an accident.

However, Mr Toure was pronounced dead on arrival.

The individuals subsequently deposited his body at the Ebenezer Mortuary at Tafo in Kumasi and fled.

The Police said investigations into the circumstances surrounding his death led to the arrest of two suspects, identified as 32-year-old Nigerien national Salifu Walid and 24-year-old Burkinabe national Aziz Wadrago Mane.

The two were arrested on September 20, 2026, at their hideout at Banpanase, near Mamponteng in the Ashanti Region.

Preliminary investigations have established that the suspects are members of a four-member group believed to have masterminded the kidnapping and murder of the Senegalese goalkeeper.

The group allegedly posed as football scout agents and used online platforms to lure unsuspecting victims into Ghana.

During interrogation, the two suspects reportedly admitted their involvement in the crime and provided information about their respective roles in luring Mr Toure to Ghana as part of an alleged scheme to defraud him.

The Police are now intensifying efforts to arrest two other suspects, identified as Noukoubri Arzouma Sylviain, also known as Prince Pierre, and Barry.

The two suspects are currently on the run and are believed to have played central roles in the activities of the group.

Salifu Walid and Aziz Wadrago Mane remain in Police custody and will be processed for court.

The Ghana Police Service said investigations are continuing as efforts are made to apprehend the remaining suspects.

Ghana News.title: TVET Service, Bank of Ghana explore partnership to boost skills development
Ghana News.content:
The management of the Ghana TVET Service, led by its Director-General, Engr. Dr Eric Kofi Adzroe, has paid a courtesy call on the Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, at the Bank’s headquarters in Accra to advance discussions on the country’s skills development agenda and explore a strategic partnership that places technical and vocational education at the center of Ghana’s economic transformation.

The engagement focused on the role of sustained investment in Technical and Vocational Education and Training in shaping national productivity, enterprise development and employment outcomes. Both institutions recognised that the quality, relevance and reach of skills training will be decisive in determining how many Ghanaians are able to access meaningful work, build viable enterprises and contribute to economic growth, particularly at a time when the structure of work itself is undergoing significant change.

The discussions were framed within the context of a shifting global labour market, where automation, artificial intelligence and digital technologies are redefining the requirements of industry.

According to the Service, increasingly, employers are prioritising demonstrated competence over formal credentials, placing emphasis on practical skills, adaptability and the ability to apply knowledge in real-world settings. For Ghana, this shift presents both a challenge and an opportunity. A workforce that is trained, certified and aligned to industry needs strengthens productivity, attracts investment and expands the country’s economic base, while also offering a credible pathway for addressing unemployment through enterprise creation and self-employment.

Speaking during the meeting, the Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, underscored the economic value of skills development, describing it as an investment with far-reaching returns.

"Every skilled Ghanaian is a business waiting to happen. When we invest in TVET, we are not just training workers; we are equipping job creators, and every enterprise a graduate launches strengthens the economic fabric of this nation," he said.

The Governor further underscored the importance of broadening access to certification as a means of unlocking the full potential of Ghana’s workforce.

He noted that a significant number of Ghanaians acquire their skills through informal pathways, yet remain excluded from formal economic opportunities due to the absence of recognised certification.

"Certification must move beyond the walls of our formal institutions. Thousands of Ghanaians learned their trades through informal apprenticeships, master craftsmen passing skills to eager hands, yet their talent remains undocumented and undervalued. Certifying their skills validates their talent and opens doors to formal jobs, credit, contracts and careers previously out of reach," he said.

Responding on behalf of the Ghana TVET Service, the Director-General, Engr. Dr Eric Kofi Adzroe, emphasised the central role of skills in driving inclusive growth and economic resilience, stressing the need to align training delivery with the evolving demands of industry.

"When a young person acquires a skill, they acquire the power to create a job for themselves and for others. That is the most reliable engine of inclusive growth this country has," Dr. Adzroe said.

Also contributing to the discussions, the Deputy Director-General in charge of Management Services, Mr Abdul Fatah Maigah Mahama Esq, drew attention to the pace at which the world of work is changing and the implications for skills development.

"The world of work is transforming faster than any of us have seen before. Automation, artificial intelligence and digital technologies are rewriting the job descriptions of entire industries, and the workers who will thrive are those with the practical, adaptable skills that TVET delivers," Fatah Mahama noted.

The visit also served to formally invite the Governor of the Bank of Ghana to participate in the National TVET Week 2026 celebrations scheduled for 12 to 16 October. The week-long programme will convene stakeholders from government, industry, development partners and civil society to examine the future of skills development in Ghana and outline practical steps towards building a workforce that is responsive to emerging economic demands.

Beyond dialogue, the engagement signals a deliberate effort to position skills development at the core of national economic policy. With the Governor expected to deliver a keynote address at the policy dialogue during National TVET Week, the collaboration reflects a growing alignment between Ghana’s financial leadership and its skills development agenda, reinforcing the role of TVET as a key driver of productivity, enterprise growth and long-term economic transformation.

Ghana News.title: Ghana TVET Service, OR Foundation partner to promote sustainable fashion
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana TVET Service has partnered with the OR Foundation to promote sustainable fashion and circular design as part of National TVET Week 2026.

The partnership will feature the Next Gen Fashion Icon Showcase, which will give Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) learners a platform to demonstrate their skills in designing and producing garments from discarded materials.

The initiative seeks to introduce circular design and sustainable fashion more prominently into skills training while highlighting opportunities within Ghana’s growing creative and textile sectors.

Director-General of the Ghana TVET Service, Engr. Dr Eric Kofi Adzroe, said the showcase would help change perceptions about waste and demonstrate the practical skills of TVET learners.

“The fashion show gives every Ghanaian the chance to witness, first hand, what our learners are capable of. When people see garments made from what was once thrown away, they begin to look at their surroundings differently.”

He said the initiative would also encourage people to view discarded materials as potential resources.

Deputy Director-General in charge of Management Services, Abdul Fatah Maigah Mahama, said the partnership should inform broader changes to TVET curriculum.

“This partnership raises a bigger conversation than one event. It challenges us to look at our curriculum design itself and ask whether sustainability is treated as an add-on or as a core competency.”

He said sustainability should be incorporated across different areas of technical and vocational training.

Dr Adzroe also said the collaboration would expose learners to new approaches to upcycling and circular design through training from instructors associated with The OR Foundation.

The OR Foundation’s Co-Founder and Executive Director, Elizabeth Ricketts, said Ghana has the potential to play a leading role in sustainable fashion.

“When it comes to sustainable fashion, Ghana has so much to teach the world. At The OR Foundation, our goal is to ensure that young people interested in circularity, alongside creative entrepreneurs already pioneering circular practices, have access to the institutional support, training, and business development they need to thrive.”

The OR Foundation has worked in Ghana’s textile sector, including initiatives focused on young designers, upcycling and livelihoods within the second-hand clothing industry.

The partnership comes against the backdrop of concerns over textile waste, particularly in areas such as Kantamanto, where discarded clothing is repaired, repurposed and resold.

The Next Gen Fashion Icon Showcase will form part of National TVET Week, scheduled for October 12 to 16, 2026.

The week is expected to bring together government, industry, development partners and civil society organisations to discuss skills development and emerging opportunities within Ghana’s economy.

Ghana News.title: Achimota, Accra Academy, PRESEC Osu qualify for next stage of National Public Speaking Event
Ghana News.content:
The Greater Accra National Public Speaking Event held at PRESEC Legon saw Achimota School, Accra Academy, and PRESEC Osu emerge as the winners and secure their places in the next stage of the competition.

The topic focused on drug abuse, a significant issue that Ghana is currently working to address. Drug abuse refers to the harmful or improper use of legal or illegal substances.

The students highlighted the various dangers associated with drug abuse, including sudden mood swings, secrecy, loss of interest in school, addiction, and potential long-term damage to the brain and other vital organs.

Through their presentations, the students expressed their concerns about drug abuse and created awareness about its harmful effects, particularly on young people and students.

They also enlightened the audience on possible ways to address the issue, presenting practical solutions to help individuals struggling with substance abuse and prevent others from becoming involved.

Overall, the public speaking event was an interesting, impactful, and insightful experience that encouraged students to speak confidently about an important social issue while educating the audience on the dangers of drug abuse.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
