Health spending per capita in Mexico — including government spending and individual spending — was US $1,588 in 2024, according to the OECD.

The OECD average was 275% higher at $5,967.

Among 49 countries included in the “Health at a Glance 2025” report, Mexico ranked 43rd on this measure, placing it in the second lowest decile.

Has Mexico improved on this indicator over the past decade?

Yes and no.

According to the OECD, health expenditure per capita grew 1.6% annually in real terms between 2014 and 2018 and 2.1% annually in real terms between 2019 and 2024. The latter period, during which the annual growth rate was 0.5 percentage points higher, corresponds to the six-year term of former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador.

In 2016, health spending per capita in Mexico was US $1,080, according to the OECD.

The OECD average that year was 271% higher at $4,003. Thus, the difference between per capita health spending in Mexico and the OECD average was slightly lower in 2016 than in 2024.

In 2016, Mexico ranked 39th out of 44 countries assessed by the OECD, placing it in the second lowest decile.

HOSPITAL BEDS PER 1,000 PEOPLE (bottom decile)

In 2023, Mexico had just one hospital bed per 1,000 people, according to the OECD.

The OECD average was significantly higher at 4.2 beds per 1,000 people.

Among 44 countries included in the “Health at a Glance 2025” report, Mexico ranked last, placing it in the bottom decile.

Has Mexico improved on this indicator over the past decade?

No, but it has worsened either.

The number of beds per 1,000 people in Mexico in 2023 was unchanged from a decade earlier, according to the OECD.

The federal government is aiming to increase the number of public hospital beds in Mexico by 9,139 during its six-year term (October 2024 to September 2030), but in a country of some 130 million people, the achievement of that goal would not significantly change the national ratio.

SATISFACTION WITH AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY HEALTHCARE (third lowest decile)

The results of a 2023 Gallup World Poll included in the OECD’s “Health at a Glance 2025” report show that 56% of Mexicans are satisfied with the availability of quality healthcare in the area where they live.

The OECD average was eight points higher at 64%.

Among the 38 countries included in the OECD report, Mexico ranked 27th, placing it in the third lowest decile.

Has Mexico improved on this indicator over the past decade?

Yes, but only marginally.

The percentage of Mexicans who were satisfied with the availability of quality healthcare in the area where they live was 55% in 2014.

The overall picture

FURTHER READING:

The OECD’s “Health at a Glance 2025” country note for Mexico was a primary source for this article. It includes additional health and healthcare indicators not included in this report.

A 2025 report (Spanish) by the Mexico City-based think tank Fundar includes a number of recommendations aimed at improving health and healthcare in Mexico. Among its recommendations are to “promote a culture of prevention” and increase funding for all public health institutions.

This World Bank document outlines “several persistent challenges that have historically constrained Mexico’s progress” toward achieving universal health coverage.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Mexico’s population surpasses 130 million even as fertility rate falls
World.content:
Listen to this article

Mexico’s population was just over 130.9 million in late 2025, an increase of almost 4% compared to five years earlier, according to the National Institute of Statistics and Geography (INEGI).

The estimated population figure is among the findings of INEGI’s 2025 Intercensal Survey, conducted last October and November at more than 7.3 million homes across Mexico.

Among the other key findings of the survey — whose results were published on Tuesday — are that Mexico’s population growth has slowed, the median age of the population has risen and the fertility rate has declined.

Mexico’s population approaches 131 million

INEGI reported that Mexico’s population was 130,911,314 (130.91 million) in late 2025.

That figure represents an increase of 3.9% compared to the 126.01 million people counted when INEGI conducted Mexico’s most recent census in 2020.

Of Mexico’s 130.9 million people, 51.9% are female and 48.1% are male.

Just 0.9% of Mexico’s population was born in a foreign country, according to INEGI. Of the 1.17 million residents born outside Mexico, 57.1% — 668,658 people — were born in the United States, INEGI said.

The next largest cohorts of foreign-born residents are natives of Venezuela, Cuba and Guatemala.

Annual population growth falls below 1%

INEGI reported that the number of people who live in private dwellings in Mexico — around 99.6% of the population — increased by an average of 0.7% per year between the 2020 Census and the 2025 Intercensal Survey.

Average annual population growth in the 2020-25 period was 0.3 percentage points lower than the average yearly growth recorded between 2015 and 2020.

Mexico’s median age rises above 30

INEGI reported that Mexico’s median age was 32 in 2025, up from 29 in 2020.

In other words, half of Mexico’s population is 32 or younger and the other half is 33 or older.

Mexico’s median age is now 10 years higher than it was in 2000.

INEGI reported that the increase in Mexico’s median age was “accompanied by a relative decline in the younger age groups and a greater share of adults and older adults in the national demographic composition.”

A graph included in INEGI’s survey results report shows that 29.8% of Mexico’s population is aged 19 and below.

Fertility rate declines sharply

INEGI reported that Mexico’s total fertility rate was 1.2 in 2024, down from 1.9 in 2019. Mexico City had the lowest fertility rate in the country at 0.8, while Chiapas had the highest at 1.8.

Mexico’s population will decline in the coming decades if its fertility rate doesn’t rise and immigration doesn’t increase significantly.

According to Our World in Data, the replacement-level fertility rate (the total fertility rate needed to keep the population size stable overtime, without migration) is commonly stated to be 2.1.”

“But the level can vary based on the sex ratio, child mortality rates, and other factors,” adds the data-focused website.

At her Wednesday morning press conference, President Claudia Sheinbaum acknowledged that Mexico’s fertility and population growth rates are falling. She noted that many Mexicans are having children (or just one child) later in life or deciding not to have children at all.

Sheinbaum highlighted that the phenomenon is not “exclusive” to Mexico, but rather something that is happening in countries around the world.

The federal Finance Ministry noted in a recent budget document that demographic changes in Mexico could cause the taxpayer base to decline in the coming years at a time when senior pension obligations are higher.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: What to Do in São Paulo in Late September 2026: Festivals, Don Carlo’s Finale and the Boat Show
World.content:
Culture

Key Facts —Festival weekend. Oktoberfest at Ibirapuera, the Italian Festa de San Gennaro in Mooca and the free Feira Gosto.SA all run on 26–27 September. —Opera finale. Verdi’s “Don Carlo” closes at the Theatro Municipal on Saturday — its first Brazilian staging in twenty years. —Indie double bill. Balaclava Fest takes Tokio Marine Hall for two days, with Blonde Redhead, DIIV and Beach Fossils. —Big rooms. The Boat Show runs at São Paulo Expo through Tuesday, and Samuel Rosa meets the São Paulo Big Band at Sala São Paulo on Saturday night. —October stacked. Zayn, Robbie Williams, the Pussycat Dolls, Iron Maiden and three BTS stadium nights are already on next month’s calendar.

If you are wondering what to do in São Paulo in the last week of September, the answer is almost too much: Sao Paulo in September 2026 ends with a festival weekend, an opera finale and two very different big nights out.

Spring arrived this week, and the city is spending its first warm weekend outdoors. Three festivals share the calendar, and most of the street events cost nothing.

The quiet catch is October. São Paulo’s concert promoters have packed next month with stadium and club shows, and several are already close to sold out. The preview below lists what to book now.

Sao Paulo in September: the final week

Thursday 24 – Tuesday 29 September São Paulo Boat Show, 29th edition São Paulo Expo, Rodovia dos Imigrantes · Tickets via Sympla; children under one metre enter free Latin America’s largest nautical event gathers some 300 exhibitors for six days of launches — a snapshot of Brazil’s coastal lifestyle economy, even for non-sailors. Our full guide.

Friday 25 – Sunday 27 September (Fridays to Sundays through 4 October) São Paulo Oktoberfest at Ibirapuera Arena de Eventos, Parque Ibirapuera · Paid entry via the official site and Ticketmaster Brasil; Fridays 5–11 p.m., weekends 2–11 p.m. Three weekends of brass bands, long tables and German-style beer in the city’s central park — the season’s most homesickness-proof outing for German-speaking expats. Our full guide.

Saturday 26 September, 7 p.m. Verdi’s “Don Carlo” — final performance Theatro Municipal, Praça Ramos de Azevedo, Centro · Price from the theatre The opera’s first Brazilian staging in twenty years closes on Saturday, with American soprano Ailyn Pérez and Brazilian tenor Atalla Ayan in the cast. Opera needs no Portuguese.

Saturday 26 September, 9 p.m. Samuel Rosa and Joyce Alane with the São Paulo Big Band Sala São Paulo, Praça Júlio Prestes · Price from the venue The “Encontros Históricos” series puts one of Brazil’s best-loved rock voices in front of a big band, inside one of the world’s finest concert halls.

Saturday 26 – Sunday 27 September, from 3 p.m. Balaclava Fest, 16th edition Tokio Marine Hall, Santo Amaro · Tickets via Ingresse · over-16s only The indie festival doubles to two days for the first time: Blonde Redhead headline Saturday, DIIV and Beach Fossils share Sunday, sixteen acts across two staggered stages. Our full guide.

Saturday 26 – Sunday 27 September, 11 a.m.–7 p.m. (Sunday to 6 p.m.) Feira Gosto.SA — Finíssima Caipira Unibes Cultural, Rua Oscar Freire 2500, Sumaré · Free entry; food paid at the stalls Some sixty exhibitors celebrate São Paulo’s country cooking — corn dishes, quirera fritters, paçoca workshops — one step from Sumaré metro station.

Saturday 26 – Sunday 27 September, from 5 p.m. 53rd Festa de San Gennaro Ruas San Gennaro and Lins, Mooca · Street area free; the cantina is ticketed separately The Italian-Brazilian street festival turns the Mooca district into a slice of Naples — fogazza, pasta and live music, a short walk from Bresser-Mooca metro.

Saturday 26 – Sunday 27 September, 11 a.m. (final weekend) Beatles Para Crianças — A Minha Banda de Rock Teatro Multiplan MorumbiShopping · Tickets via Sympla A morning Beatles show built for children, with unusual instruments and on-stage participation — an easy family hour before lunch.

Weekend sessions through September “O Musical dos Musicais” — a Broadway and West End tribute Teatro Liberdade · Tickets via Sympla Twenty performers run through numbers from “Matilda”, “Wicked” and “Mean Girls” in Kids and Teens versions — the songs need no translation.

Sao Paulo in September: the big exhibitions

Through 31 January 2027 MASP: “Histórias latino-americanas” MASP, Avenida Paulista 1578 · Paid entry; free days midweek — check masp.org.br The museum’s most ambitious show of the decade fills five floors with Latin American art from Mexico to Argentina. Our full story.

Through 24 January 2027 MAM: 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art Museu de Arte Moderna, Parque Ibirapuera · Regular museum ticket Brazil’s most traditional survey of contemporary art asks what art can still do “after everything has been said”. Pairs naturally with a park walk. Our full story.

Through 7 February 2027 IMS Paulista: Fernando Lemos retrospective Instituto Moreira Salles, Avenida Paulista 2424 · Free Some 400 works mark the centenary of the Portuguese-Brazilian surrealist photographer — and the building adds a library, café and rooftop view over Paulista.

Now showing Pinacoteca: Beatriz Milhazes Pinacoteca, Luz district · Price from the venue — check pinacoteca.org.br for the current building and tickets A solo show for one of Brazil’s central contemporary painters, all colour, rhythm and ornament — combine it with the Museu da Língua Portuguesa next door.

Sunday 27 September, all day Free Sunday: markets and a car-free Paulista Liberdade, Pari and Avenida Paulista · Free Start at the Feirinha da Liberdade for Asian street food, detour to the Bolivian Feira da Kantuta in Pari, then walk a traffic-free Avenida Paulista past Japan House and Itaú Cultural.

October preview: what to book now

3 October Sonata Arctica Audio Club, Barra Funda · Tickets via Clube do Ingresso Finnish power metal veterans in a 3,000-capacity club instead of a festival field. Details.

3 October – 1 November “Miraculous Ladybug: O Show Musical” Teatro VillaLobos, Shopping VillaLobos · Tickets via Sympla The animated hit’s official stage musical arrives for a month — the family option of the season, built on spectacle rather than dialogue.

10 October Zayn — Konnakol Tour Nubank Parque · Tickets via Ticketmaster Brasil The former One Direction singer’s first solo show in Brazil, a decade in the waiting. Details.

13 October Robbie Williams — Britpop tour Nubank Parque · R$195–690 (about US$37–130), via Ingresse His first Brazilian show in twenty years — two hours of one of Britain’s great entertainers. Details.

15 – 29 October 50th Mostra Internacional de Cinema Cinemas across São Paulo · 2026 prices pending; single tickets were R$26–32 (US$5–6) last year The city’s main annual window on world cinema turns fifty — passes traditionally sell out fast. Details.

16 October Dionne Warwick — Over and Out farewell tour Vibra São Paulo · From R$165 (about US$30), via Ticket360 A last chance to see a six-Grammy legend who has loved Brazil back for decades. Details.

20 October Pussycat Dolls — PCD Forever Tour Nubank Parque · Tickets via Eventim The reunited group’s only announced Brazilian show — 2000s pop nostalgia at open-air scale. Details.

23 October Kneecap Cine Joia, Barra Funda · Tickets via Ingresse The Belfast trio behind the BAFTA-winning film, rapping in Irish in a 700-capacity room. Details.

25 and 27 October Iron Maiden — Run For Your Lives Nubank Parque · Tickets via Livepass Fifty years of Eddie across two São Paulo nights — the metal event of the year in the band’s most loyal market. Details.

28, 30 and 31 October BTS — Arirang World Tour MorumBIS stadium · Tickets via Ticketmaster Brasil Three stadium nights, seven years in the waiting — the largest K-pop production ever booked in South America. Details.

30 October Jorja Smith Espaço Unimed, Barra Funda · Tickets via Tickets For Fun One of Britain’s finest modern soul voices in a mid-size room. Details.

31 October The Rasmus Carioca Club, Pinheiros · Tickets via Uhuu “In the Shadows” on Halloween night, in one of the city’s classic rock clubs. Details.

Further ahead: November and December

November brings the city’s biggest goodbye: Sepultura play the final concert of their 42-year career at Pacaembu on 7 November (from R$150, about US$28), one week after the Formula 1 São Paulo Grand Prix at Interlagos on 6–8 November. Ty Segall finally makes his Brazil debut at Audio Club on 15 November, Best of Blues and Rock takes Ibirapuera on 20–22 November, and the month closes with Of Monsters and Men and Babymetal. December then stacks CCXP (3–6 December) and Primavera Sound with Gorillaz and The Strokes (5–6 December) into one week.

What is on in São Paulo on the last weekend of September 2026?

The weekend of 26–27 September stacks São Paulo Oktoberfest at Ibirapuera, the free Feira Gosto.SA in Sumaré, the Festa de San Gennaro in Mooca and two days of Balaclava Fest, plus the final performance of Verdi’s “Don Carlo” and Samuel Rosa with the São Paulo Big Band on Saturday night.

What can I do in Sao Paulo in September for free?

Free options this week include the Feira Gosto.SA food fair, the street area of the Festa de San Gennaro, the Fernando Lemos retrospective at IMS Paulista, the Feirinha da Liberdade, the Feira da Kantuta and a car-free Avenida Paulista on Sunday.

Which big concerts come to São Paulo in October 2026?

October brings Zayn, Robbie Williams, the Pussycat Dolls and Iron Maiden to Nubank Parque, three BTS nights at MorumBIS, Dionne Warwick’s farewell at Vibra São Paulo, and club shows by Sonata Arctica, Kneecap, Jorja Smith and The Rasmus.

World.title: Operation Iron in Cali: 1,200 Officers, 101 Raids, 80 Arrests
World.content:
COLOMBIA · SECURITY

Key Facts — Where this is Cali is Colombia’s third-largest city and the capital of Valle del Cauca, in the country’s south-west.

— What happened More than 1,200 uniformed personnel from the National Police and the Army moved into the city before dawn.

— The numbers Officials reported 101 planned searches, 83 arrest warrants and 80 people detained.

— Where exactly Six communes, 15 neighbourhoods and 24 micro-territories, including El Calvario, San Pascual and Sucre in the centre.

— The catch Arrests are not convictions, and a single night does not dislodge a criminal economy.

— Why it counts President Abelardo de la Espriella took office in August and has made visible security operations his signature.

Before dawn on Thursday, armoured vehicles went into central Cali — the largest single security push of the new government so far.

Operation Iron in Cali began at about 3.20 a.m. on 24 September 2026. More than 1,200 police and soldiers went into six communes, and officials reported 101 searches and 80 arrests.

Cali, Colombia’s third-largest city, where the operation covered six communes (Photo: Neoredacturus, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

What happened before dawn

The operation began at roughly 3.20 a.m. on Thursday 24 September 2026. Armoured vehicles moved into central Cali alongside police and army units.

Officials put the deployment at more than 1,200 uniformed personnel. That is a large number for a single city on a single night.

The searches were executed simultaneously rather than in sequence. That is the standard design when a network is expected to warn its own members.

Reported results were 101 planned searches, 83 arrest warrants and 80 people detained.

Colombian forces call this a simultaneous intervention. The aim is to take a whole set of addresses off the board in one movement.

What Operation Iron in Cali was aimed at

The stated targets were drug-selling points, known in Colombia as ollas, and extortion networks.

Extortion is the part that reaches ordinary people. Shopkeepers, small businesses and young people were named as those affected.

The geography was specific: six communes, 15 neighbourhoods and 24 micro-territories. El Calvario, San Pascual and Sucre, in the city centre, were among them.

Those central neighbourhoods have long been associated with open drug markets. They are also where the city’s commerce is densest.

Extortion in Colombia is often called vacuna, a weekly payment for being left alone. It is the most corrosive of the crimes named.

Breaking the collection is harder than making arrests. The payment survives as long as the threat behind it is credible.

Who Cali is, for readers who do not know it

Cali is Colombia’s third-largest city, after Bogotá and Medellín, and the capital of Valle del Cauca department in the south-west.

It sits on the corridor between the Andes and the Pacific coast. That position has made it a logistics hub for legitimate trade and for cocaine alike.

The city is also the centre of Colombia’s Afro-Colombian population and of its salsa culture. Neither fact is decoration here.

Cali’s security problems are concentrated, not general. Most of the city is not a battleground, and visitors rarely see any of this.

About 2.2 million people live in the city. It is a working industrial centre as much as a cultural one.

The political frame

Abelardo de la Espriella became president of Colombia in August 2026. He campaigned on a hard security line and has governed on it.

He announced the Cali operation himself, saying the government would “liberate Cali and the whole country”.

Presidents announcing police operations personally is a choice, not a formality. It ties the government’s standing to what happens next in those neighbourhoods.

That is the risk as well as the point. Visible operations are judged on whether the streets stay changed.

His predecessor pursued negotiated settlements with armed groups. The contrast is the point of operations like this one.

What it does not mean

Eighty arrests is not eighty convictions. Colombian prosecutors must now present cases, and detentions can be overturned at first hearing.

A night of raids does not end an extortion economy. Those networks regenerate unless the prosecutions hold and the corners stay policed.

Nor does the operation say anything about the rest of Colombia. It was designed for six communes of one city.

The honest measure will be arrests that survive court, and whether merchants stop paying.

Colombia has seen large urban operations before, under several governments. Some held, and some did not.

What this means for residents and visitors

For foreign residents in Cali, the immediate effect is disruption rather than danger: closed streets, checkpoints and a visible army presence.

No travel restriction or curfew was reported. The affected areas are central, which is where some hotels and businesses sit.

For businesses, the relevant question is extortion. If the networks that collect from shopkeepers are disrupted, that shows up in operating costs.

For investors watching Colombia, this is a data point about the new government’s method, not about the economy.

Operations of this size usually thin out within days. The checkpoints go, and the question becomes what replaced the corners.

What is still not known

Officials did not publish what was seized during the searches, in drugs, cash or weapons.

No named criminal structure has been given as the principal target in the accounts available.

It is not clear how many of the 83 warrants relate to extortion rather than drug offences.

Nor has the government said what follows the raids in those neighbourhoods, which is the part that decides whether it worked.

Prosecutors have not said how many of those detained will face formal charges at their first hearing.

Frequently Asked Questions

How big was Operation Iron in Cali?

More than 1,200 police and soldiers took part. Officials reported 101 planned searches, 83 arrest warrants and 80 detentions.

Is Cali safe to visit after this?

No travel restriction or curfew was reported. The operation was concentrated in six communes, including central neighbourhoods.

Who ordered the operation?

President Abelardo de la Espriella announced it himself. He took office in August 2026 on a hard security platform.

World.title: What to Do in Rio in September 2026: the First Semana de Arte and Nine Free Things
World.content:
Rio de Janeiro · Culture

The first Semana de Arte do Rio runs to the 27th, the harp festival plays the CCBB free at lunchtime every weekday until it closes, and Zélia Duncan, Marcelo D2, Teresa Cristina and Seal take the big rooms. Here is the rest of September, day by day.

RIO DE JANEIRO — There is a great deal to do in Rio in September, and very little of it is written down anywhere in English. This guide is the monthly selection for people who live here rather than visit: what is on, where, when, what it costs, and why it might be worth crossing the city for. Most of the entries below are free.

Rock in Rio and the MIMO weekend are behind us. What remains of the month is better distributed and cheaper: until the 27th, the first Semana de Arte do Rio pulls more than ten festivals under a single banner, and the harp festival inside it gives free concerts at the CCBB at 12.30pm and 3pm every weekday to the close. After that the month belongs to Zélia Duncan, Marcelo D2, Teresa Cristina and the orchestras, with free concerts under the Arcos da Lapa on the final weekend. Plan accordingly.

Also running now

Nicole Musafir’s Pra Quem Não Me Conhece opens at the Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim. (Photo: Elisa Maciel)

Until 27 September, Fridays and Saturdays 8pm, Sundays 7pm A Pequena Prisão Teatro Laura Alvim, Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim, Av. Vieira Souto 176, Ipanema · R$30–60 · 60 minutes · 16+ Nine performances only, after more than forty at the Teatro Poeira. Vino Fragoso plays over thirty characters in the first stage adaptation of Igor Mendes’s book on the Brazilian prison system. In Portuguese, and physical enough to follow without it.

Thursday 24 September, 7pm Nicole Musafir — Pra Quem Não Me Conhece Casa de Cultura Laura Alvim, Ipanema · Price from the venue This is a short run of a one-woman show. Musafir built it out of the diaries she has kept since she was six. Blocked creatively for years, she went through the box and put what she found on stage; pianist Ceci Nery accompanies, with musical direction by Leo Valor. In Portuguese, and personal enough to reward the effort if you can follow it.

Photo: Divulgação

Until 27 September 19º Niterói em Cena — International Theatre Festival Theatro Municipal de Niterói and venues across the city · Free Paulo Betti opens with his monologue Autobiografia Autorizada. What follows is free for seventeen days: companies from Angola, Georgia, Senegal, Mexico, Colombia, Paraguay and Peru, plus street theatre on the Praça João Saldanha. The street programme — clowning, acrobatics, the Peruvian Inka Clown Show — needs no language at all. Twenty minutes on the ferry from Praça Quinze.

Every Saturday, from midnight Rock-blues at the Bukowski, the oldest rock bar in the city Bar Bukowski, Rua Álvaro Ramos 270, Botafogo · R$39.90 at the door, free from 1am on the guest list Botafogo’s Bukowski has been a rock house for decades and has just added a weekly blues night. The Charles Zanol Trio plays from midnight: Zanol has thirty years of blues, rockabilly and country behind him, with Pedro Leão on guitar and Dawton Mendes on drums and cajón. R$39.90 at the door includes a drink if you arrive before 10pm; R$99.90 gives you R$80 back in food and drink. Put your name on the guest list through @barbukowski and entry is free from 1am. The bar runs from 7pm to 5am.

To 27 September: the first Semana de Arte do Rio

Until 27 September Semana de Arte do Rio — first edition Museums, cultural centres, theatres and galleries across the city · Varies; much of it free More than ten festivals come under one banner for the first time. In addition, there are exhibitions, street interventions and events in both public and private venues. Part of the Centro Cultural Justiça Federal programme falls inside it. If you have one week of Rio in September to give to the city’s art scene, make it this one.

Thursday 24 and Friday 25 September, 12.30pm and 3pm Harp at lunchtime: two weekdays at the CCBB Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, third-floor auditorium, Centro · Free The quiet middle of the festival, and the easiest thing on this list to walk into on a working day. Nicolas Almada and Letícia Rodriguez sing Uruguayan candombe and milonga on the 24th; the Paraguayan Júlio César Villaalta takes the 24th and 25th, and the Venezuelan Luis Castro the 25th. A hundred and six seats, sung in Spanish or not sung at all.

24 to 27 September Mostra Violas Brasileiras: Da Raiz ao Contemporâneo Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Centro · Free Curated by Ivan Viela. The viola caipira is the instrument most foreigners never hear in Rio, because it belongs to the interior. Four days to correct that.

Saturday 26 and Sunday 27 September, 1pm and 3pm The RioHarpFestival closes at the CCBB Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, ground-floor rotunda and third-floor auditorium, Centro · Free Harold Emert’s Camerata Viva Música takes the rotunda on the Saturday with the Venezuelan harpist Luis Castro. On the Sunday a bagpipe band closes the Latin American edition at 1pm — gaitas de foles under Maestro J. Paulo, which is not a sentence anyone expects to read about Rio — and Castro plays the last recital upstairs at 3pm with the Japanese musician Michinari Usuda.

Late September

A scene from La Llorona — the Guatemalan Golden Globe nominee opens the Soy Loco por Ti, Centroamérica series at the CCBB Rio. (Photo: CCBB Rio / A Dois Comunicação)

Wednesday 23 September to 19 October Soy Loco por Ti, Centroamérica — Central American cinema at the CCBB Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, Centro · Free Twenty-one features and shorts from Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama, most of them never before screened in Brazil: the Locarno winner Tengo sueños eléctricos, the Cannes Caméra d’Or winner Nuestras Madres and La Llorona, the first Central American film nominated for a Golden Globe. A masterclass with curator Laura Bermúdez follows the opening on 26 September, and a Central American documentary debate on 30 September.

Thursday 24 September, 8pm Aguidavi do Jêje, with Chico César, Gilsons and Pretinho da Serrinha Circo Voador, Lapa · R$70 (half price) The Tocantins singer-songwriter’s biggest Rio date yet, with guests spanning generations: Chico César, the Gilsons, Pretinho da Serrinha and Carlinhos 7 Cordas.

Thursday 24 September, 8pm Marcelo D2 at Rio Gastronomia Jockey Club Brasileiro, Rua Jardim Botânico 1003, Gávea · R$40 (half price) The rapper closes a week of food-and-music programming at the Jockey Club’s food festival, with the Botafogo and Corcovado views thrown in. Eat first; he goes on at eight.

Friday 25 September, 7pm Zélia Duncan at Vivo Rio Av. Infante Dom Henrique 85, Parque do Flamengo · From R$60 (half price) The singer in full band at the Flamengo park auditorium — the month’s biggest room dedicated to Brazilian song.

Friday 25 September, 7.30pm and 9.30pm Itsáry opens at night: a four-hands dinner with Bernabé Simón Padrós Itsáry, Rua Franklin Roosevelt 194A, Centro · R$420, or R$650 with the wine pairing A restaurant in Centro that normally serves only lunch is opening after dark once a month for a guest chef. First is the Argentine Bernabé Simón Padrós of Emile in Copacabana, who has cooked at Central in Lima and at Astrid y Gastón. The menu the two chefs built together runs from a small gazpacho of cavaca and melon through corn ravioli with parmesan from Alagoa to grilled pork cheek, and ends on chocolate, cashew and passion fruit. Two sittings, booking on (21) 96640-9089 or through @itsary.rio. Romano Fontanive of Gabbiano cooks the October dinner.

Friday 25 September, 8pm Cachorro Grande and Vanguart at the Circo Voador Lapa · R$70 (half price) A Porto Alegre rock double bill: Cachorro Grande’s retro-groove with Vanguart’s psychedelia, in the Lapa tent on a Friday.

Friday 25 September, 8.30pm Baile Charme de Madureira at the Capanema Palácio Gustavo Capanema, Rua da Imprensa 16, Centro · Free Twelve years of the charm baile that put Madureira’s black-music scene on the national map, played free in the Capanema forecourt as part of the Próxima Parada festival.

Saturday 26 September Seal — 30 years Qualistage, Barra da Tijuca · Price from the venue The thirtieth-anniversary tour. A large, comfortable room and a set of songs most people in it will know by heart.

Saturday 26 September, 6pm Tribute to Luiz Carlos de Moura Castro — Palácio São Clemente Portuguese Consulate, Rua São Clemente 424, Botafogo · Free Martin Almeida at the piano, with Jesús Suárez on harp, in a posthumous tribute to the pianist who was a long-standing partner of the series. The consulate residence opens for it, which is reason enough to go.

Saturday 26 September, 7.30pm Petrobras Symphony honours Moacir Santos, then Hamilton de Holanda Praça dos Arcos, Arcos da Lapa · Free The Orquestra Petrobras Sinfônica plays the great composer-arranger’s orchestral music with Fabiana Cozza and Marcos Sacramento, and Hamilton de Holanda’s trio closes the night. Free, under the arches.

Saturday 26 September, 8pm Ave Sangria, Papangu and Zepelim at the Circo Voador Lapa · R$80 (half price) Pernambuco psych-rock from the 1970s — Ave Sangria, reformed and on form — with Recife’s current experimentalists Papangu. The month’s best double bill for guitar music.

Sunday 27 September, 4pm Festival Solar: a tribute to Ney Matogrosso Praça dos Arcos, Arcos da Lapa · Free Juliana Linhares, Linn da Quebrada, MC Tha, Tássia Reis and Xênia França take on the maestro’s repertoire — the most interesting free bill of the closing weekend, and the last big day of the Semana de Arte.

Tuesday 29 September, 6pm Recorders and voices at the Forte de Copacabana Museu do Exército, Forte de Copacabana, Praça Cel. Eugênio Franco 1, Posto 6 · Free The recorder ensemble Fino Som and the vocal group Vozes Encanto play international classics, directed by Nelma Pataro. The fort sits on the rocks at the end of Copacabana beach and the view alone carries the evening.

Wednesday 30 September, 12.30pm Mignone, 40 anos de saudade — the month closes at the CCBB Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Rua Primeiro de Março 66, 4th floor, Centro · Free Five pianists mark forty years since the death of Francisco Mignone, one of the central figures of Brazilian concert music, with video testimony from the composer between the pieces. A good last free hour of Rio in September.

Until 4 December The Jazz Room: a Sinatra and Armstrong tribute Teatro Rival Petrobras, Rua Álvaro Alvim 33, Cinelândia · From R$100 The Rival’s long-running tribute evening — the American songbook with a live band in the Art Deco theatre off Cinelândia. The reliable option when nothing else on this list fits the night.

Opera and orchestras in Rio in September

September Festival Oficina da Ópera Theatro Municipal, Cinelândia, Centro · Price from the box office The Municipal’s September strand brings Mascagni’s Cavalleria Rusticana and Donizetti’s Il Campanello. The building alone justifies the ticket; it was modelled on the Paris Opera and finished in 1909.

Through September 21st RioHarpFestival and Música no Museu Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil and partner venues · Mostly free Twenty-three harp concerts run from 16 to 27 September inside the Semana de Arte, all of them free — at the CCBB, tickets are handed out at the box office from 9am on the day. They sit alongside the Música no Museu series, which is in its twenty-ninth year and puts classical music into museums, palaces and churches at no charge. The September dates are listed individually above: the CCBB on the 9th and the 30th, the Museu Nacional de Belas Artes on the 16th, the Palácio Tiradentes on the 18th, the Palácio São Clemente on the 26th and the Forte de Copacabana on the 29th. One of the best-value things in the city and almost unknown to new arrivals.

Free all month in Rio in September

Until 12 October Vik Muniz — season extended Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Centro · Free Brazil’s most internationally recognised living visual artist, in the show that has been held over. If you see one exhibition this month, this is the one to see.

2 September to 16 November Amazônicas — Poéticas Femininas Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, Centro · Free Sissa Aneleh curates work by women from the North of Brazil. The reading is decolonial, and it foregrounds Afro-indigenous ancestry. Furthermore, the show uses virtual and augmented-reality elements.

September African Cinema showcase Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil cinemas, Centro · Free or low cost Ten features and six contemporary shorts. Given how little African cinema reaches Brazilian screens, this is the rare chance.

Until late September Coleção Ingá: Brasil Plural — final weeks Centro Cultural Justiça Federal, Centro · Free Around 200 works come from the Museu de História e Artes do Estado. Among them are Di Cavalcanti, Portinari, Goeldi and Mestre Guarany. The CCJF’s September programme also runs open-air cinema, short-film and Spanish-cinema seasons, choral concerts, flamenco, choro and indigenous music, literary workshops and two theatre productions — nearly all of it free.

Until 10 October, Tuesday to Saturday, midday to 7pm Inefável Presença — nine painters from one Tijuca studio Centro Cultural dos Correios, R. Visc. de Itaboraí 20, Centro · Free Nine artists have shared a studio in Tijuca for seven years. Ayla de Oliveira curates the show, and also exhibits in it. The group formed around a life-drawing class at the UFRJ fine arts school in 2017 and kept meeting on Monday evenings. Figurative painting, unfashionable for a while, now finding buyers.

Planning your Rio in September

Where we have not printed a ticket price, the organisers did not publish one — check with the venue before you travel. Programmes at the CCBB, the Theatro Municipal and the CCJF change during Rio in September, so confirm on the day.

This guide to Rio in September runs monthly, and returns in October. If you run a venue, a gallery or a production in Rio and would like to be considered, write to the newsroom with the date, the time, the address and the ticket price. Those four things are what get an event into the list.

More on living here: our Rio de Janeiro coverage and Expats in Brazil.

World.title: Vorcaro Property Searches Made Public as Brazil’s Top Court Lifts Secrecy
World.content:
BRAZIL · BUSINESS

Key Facts — The country Brazil is Latin America’s largest economy. Banco Master was a mid-sized bank on São Paulo’s main financial avenue.

— What happened Federal Police searched four properties linked to Daniel Vorcaro, in São Paulo, Brasília, Belo Horizonte and Nova Lima.

— What was found About R$290,000 (US$56,600) in cash in a bedroom safe, watches, armoured cars and a painting attributed to Renoir.

— Why now The detail is public because the Supreme Court lifted confidentiality on the investigation file, not because the searches are new.

— The catch Nothing here is a verdict. Seizures are evidence-gathering, and Vorcaro has not been convicted of anything.

— Why it counts Police estimate missing funds near R$12 billion (US$2.3 billion), in what the finance minister called a possible record fraud.

A wine cellar, a diamond necklace and a Renoir: the inventory from a fallen banker’s houses is now on the public record.

Details of the Vorcaro property searches became public on 24 September 2026, after Brazil’s Supreme Court lifted secrecy on the case file. Federal Police had searched homes linked to the Banco Master founder.

Avenida Faria Lima in São Paulo, where Banco Master had its offices (Photo: Wilfredor, CC0 via Wikimedia Commons)

What Banco Master was

Banco Master was a private bank with offices on Faria Lima, the avenue that serves as São Paulo’s financial district.

It sold investment notes promising unusually high returns. Federal Police describe a structure in which new deposits covered shortfalls owed to earlier customers.

Brazil’s central bank ordered the bank into extrajudicial liquidation on 18 November 2025. Subsidiaries were wound up through the months that followed.

Police estimate the missing funds may reach R$12 billion, about US$2.3 billion, and that up to 1.6 million people could be affected.

The bank’s collapse pulled in others. Banco de Brasília, a state-owned lender that had bought Master paper, took the largest declared hit.

What the Vorcaro property searches turned up

Investigators searched four properties. They were a São Paulo mansion with an underground wine cellar, plus houses in Brasília, Belo Horizonte and Nova Lima.

The Brasília property runs to about 1,699 square metres. It was bought in June 2024 for R$36 million, about US$7 million, and was made unavailable in March.

From a bedroom closet safe, police recorded about R$290,000, roughly US$56,600, in reais and dollars. They also logged watches, armoured vehicles and a six-terabyte hard drive.

The inventory includes a diamond necklace bearing the letter D and a painting attributed to Pierre-Auguste Renoir.

The documents are the part that matters

Jewellery makes headlines. Paperwork makes cases.

Police also logged documents on the letterheads of the Chamber of Deputies and of Banco de Brasília. That bank is owned by the federal district government.

Banco de Brasília has set aside more than R$5 billion, about US$977 million, against Master-related losses.

What those documents show has not been established publicly. Their existence in the file is what was disclosed, not their meaning.

Brazilian investigators routinely seize paper alongside valuables. It is the paper that later shows who paid whom, and when.

Why this became public today

The searches themselves are not new. They belong to Operação Compliance Zero, the Federal Police investigation opened when the bank was liquidated.

What changed is access. The Supreme Court lifted confidentiality on parts of the file, so the inventories could be reported.

That is a normal step in a Brazilian criminal case. It is why one day can produce a flood of detail about months-old searches.

Readers should not mistake the publication date for the event date.

The searches ran under warrants issued months ago. What arrived today was the inventory, not the raid.

Where Vorcaro stands legally

Daniel Vorcaro was detained at an airport on 17 November 2025, reportedly preparing to leave for Malta by private jet.

A federal appeals court released him on 29 November 2025. He was detained again on 4 March 2026, in a later phase of the same operation.

The investigation covers money laundering, corruption and foreign exchange offences. He has not been convicted.

Everything seized is evidence until a court says otherwise. That distinction matters more, not less, when the inventory is this colourful.

Two detentions in four months is unusual. It reflects how fast the case moved after the central bank shut the bank down.

What it means for people with money in Brazil

For depositors the protection is the Fundo Garantidor de Créditos, Brazil’s deposit insurance scheme. It covers balances up to a ceiling per person per institution.

The lesson the case keeps teaching is duller than the Renoir. Unusually high promised returns are a description of risk, not of skill.

Foreign residents holding Brazilian fixed income should know which institution actually issues a note they buy, and whether it is covered.

None of that is a comment on any bank operating today. It is what the Master file illustrates.

Deposit insurance covers deposits. It does not cover every instrument a bank sells, which is the gap this case ran through.

What is still not known

Prosecutors have not said what the seized documents establish, or whether they will lead to charges beyond those already filed.

The total value of assets frozen across the case has not been published in one figure.

Nor is there a public timetable for trial. Brazilian financial cases of this size routinely run for years.

The Vorcaro property searches add detail to a picture that is still being assembled.

Nor has any court ruled on whether the seized items were bought with money from the bank. That question sits at the centre of the case.

Frequently Asked Questions

Were the Vorcaro property searches carried out today?

No — they belong to an earlier phase of Operação Compliance Zero. On 24 September the Supreme Court lifted secrecy on the file.

What happened to Banco Master?

Brazil’s central bank ordered it into extrajudicial liquidation on 18 November 2025. Police estimate missing funds may reach R$12 billion, about US$2.3 billion.

Has Daniel Vorcaro been convicted?

No. He has been detained twice and is under investigation for money laundering, corruption and foreign exchange offences.

Sources: https://aloalobahia.com/noticias/2026/09/24/mansoes-de-daniel-vorcaro-tinham-adega-subterranea-cinema-spa-e-cofres-veja-detalhes/; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banco_Master_scandal

World.title: Vale Mina de Fábrica Restart Cleared by a Minas Gerais Court
World.content:
BRAZIL · BUSINESS

Key Facts — Where this is Mina de Fábrica is an iron ore mine at Ouro Preto, in Minas Gerais, Brazil’s mining state.

— What happened On 25 January 2026, about 263,000 cubic metres of sediment-laden water overflowed a pit into two rivers.

— The damage The state environment secretary reported lost biodiversity, silted rivers and contaminated riverbank forest. Vale said nobody was hurt.

— The decision The Minas Gerais state court allowed a partial restart, under a compliance agreement with prosecutors and the state government.

— The catch Only part of the mine restarts, and only while licences and conditions hold. Vale says output guidance is unchanged.

— Why it counts In Brazil, after Mariana and Brumadinho, a court decides when a stopped mine may run again — not the miner.

Eight months after a pit overflowed into two rivers, a state court has let Brazil’s biggest miner switch part of the site back on.

A Minas Gerais court has cleared the Vale Mina de Fábrica restart, and the company began partial operations on 23 September 2026. The mine had been shut since January, when water and sediment escaped a pit.

The hills around Ouro Preto, Minas Gerais, where Vale’s Mina de Fábrica sits (Photo: Josue Marinho, CC BY 3.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

What Vale actually announced

Vale said on 23 September 2026 that it had begun a partial resumption at Mina de Fábrica. The state court had given its authorisation.

The clearance rests on a Termo de Compromisso, a formal compliance agreement signed with Minas Gerais prosecutors and the state government.

Only part of the operation restarts. Vale must keep its licences and conditions in force and carry on with the actions the agreement sets out.

The company said the restart does not change its current production guidance.

Why the mine stopped in the first place

The mine stopped on 25 January 2026. About 263,000 cubic metres of water mixed with sediment escaped a pit at the site.

It reached the Goiabeiras and Maranhão rivers and spilled onto neighbouring ground operated by CSN Mineração.

Vale said nobody was injured. João Lobo, the state environment secretary, reported lost biodiversity, silting and damage to riverbank forest.

Those two statements are not in conflict. One is about people, the other about the river.

CSN Mineração, whose ground the water reached, is a separate miner. The overflow therefore crossed a company boundary as well as a river.

The company operates in two segments, Iron Ore Solutions and Vale Base Metals. It extracts, produces, and distributes iron ore, iron ore pellets, briquettes, nickel, copper, other ferrous…

The Vale Mina de Fábrica restart in context

Vale S.A. is a Brazilian mining company and one of the world’s largest iron ore producers. Its shares trade in São Paulo under the ticker VALE3.

The Vale Mina de Fábrica restart matters to the company’s operations, but it is not a macro event for Brazil. Vale said the partial restart does not change its current production projections.

The available reports do not give the mine’s annual capacity or tonnage. They also do not state the exact date of the TJMG decision or reproduce the full text of the court’s order.

What is clear is the legal architecture: a state court, a state prosecutor’s office and a state government, all inside Minas Gerais. The available reports do not name a federal ministry as the deciding authority.

What the conditions mean day to day

The Termo de Compromisso is not a one-off permission slip. It is an ongoing agreement, and Vale said its actions under it continue.

Vale said the actions provided for in the Termo de Compromisso will continue alongside the partial resumption. The reports reviewed do not specify which inspections, reports or checks the agreement expressly requires.

The company framed the restart as consistent with its guidance. It did not announce new spending, new jobs or a change to its sales targets.

The partial restart is not a return to full operations. Reports do not say what it does to site output.

Why this matters to expats and investors

Anyone holding Vale shares, directly or through an emerging-market fund, is exposed to Brazilian court decisions. This week’s decision is a modest positive, not a clean bill of health.

The wider signal is procedural. Here the court authorised a partial resumption under a Termo de Compromisso.

Vale, state prosecutors and the state government are all parties to that agreement.

That structure raises the cost of doing business, but it also makes outcomes more predictable for those who follow the filings. Compliance news now shapes Vale’s story alongside price headlines.

For foreign residents in Minas Gerais the read is narrow. A suspended mine is moving again under supervision, and the conditions still bind Vale.

What to watch next

The key test is whether the partial restart holds without new incidents or new court orders. Vale has not published a timeline for returning to full capacity.

Watch the Termo de Compromisso for any public updates from Minas Gerais prosecutors. Those documents, not press releases, will show what conditions are being enforced.

Watch Vale’s quarterly production reports for any mention of Mina de Fábrica. If the partial restart expands, it should appear there first.

Vale reported a partial resumption authorised by the court. It is subject to the safety, environmental and licensing conditions in its statement.

The Vale Mina de Fábrica restart is conditional, so the thing to watch is whether the conditions hold. A breach would put the clearance back before the same court.

Frequently Asked Questions

Did Vale get full approval to restart Mina de Fábrica?

No — Vale said it began a partial resumption, not a full restart. It must respect safety, environmental and licence conditions.

Which court authorized the restart?

The Tribunal de Justiça do Estado de Minas Gerais (TJMG), Minas Gerais’s state court of justice. Reports do not give the exact date of that decision.

Why was the mine halted?

A water-and-sediment overflow was recorded at the complex on 25 January 2026; TJMG suspended all mining activities there on 6 February 2026. Resumption was subject to technical proof of stability and safety.

Sources: https://diariodocomercio.com.br/negocios/vale-retoma-mina-de-fabrica/; https://br.advfn.com/jornal/2026/09/vale-inicia-retomada-parcial-da-mina-de-fabrica-apos-autorizacao-judicial

World.title: Moving to the Bahamas 2026: Residency, Costs and Island Life for Foreigners
World.content:
GUIDES · BAHAMAS

Key Facts — What it is A guide to what living in the Bahamas actually costs and what daily life looks like across Nassau, Freeport and the Family Islands, with the permit rules in summary.

— Who it’s for Remote workers, retirees and families weighing a no-income-tax archipelago against Portugal, Panama or the Cayman Islands.

— What it costs Petrol was gazetted at US$7.34 a gallon in New Providence and US$7.55 on the outer Family Islands in mid-2026. International school runs from US$13,325 to US$35,600 a year at the main international school.

— Why it matters There is no income tax, but almost everything is imported and taxed twice: customs duty first, then 10 percent value added tax on the duty-inclusive landed cost.

— The catch The United States embassy says a medical evacuation to Florida may cost in excess of US$50,000, and that payment may be demanded in advance.

Which numbers are gazetted and which are guesswork, what changed for foreign property owners on 1 July 2026, and why the electricity bill depends on which island you pick.

Moving to the Bahamas trades one kind of tax for another. There is no income tax, no capital gains tax and no inheritance tax, and the Bahamian dollar has been pegged one to one with the US dollar since 1973. In exchange, a 700-island country imports almost everything it consumes, taxes those imports at rates Washington calls among the highest in the region, and then charges value added tax on the duty-inclusive cost.

Residency, in summary

Anyone moving to the Bahamas needs authorisation from the immigration department first. The ordinary route for financially independent people and retirees is an annual residence permit, renewable each year, which does not permit work. Paid employment needs a separate work permit.

Permanent residence on economic grounds now requires a minimum investment of B$1,000,000, either in Bahamian real estate or in zero coupon bonds issued by the central bank, held for at least ten years. That figure rose from B$750,000 on 1 January 2025, and older guides still quote the old number.

A second threshold is separately misreported. Accelerated consideration, sometimes called speedy consideration, applies to buyers of a residence worth B$1,500,000 or more. It is not B$750,000, whatever the relocation sites say.

The remote work permit is the open question. The Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay, launched in 2020, is still marketed as live on the tourism ministry’s campaign site with unchanged terms. It is a one-year permit at US$1,025 for a professional and US$525 per dependant, renewable annually to a maximum of three years. No local employment is allowed and proof of medical insurance is required. But it does not appear among the permit categories on the immigration department’s own page, and the application portal did not resolve when checked on 24 September 2026. Confirm before you rely on it.

Nassau harbour. New Providence holds about three-quarters of the population and effectively all specialist healthcare and schooling (Photo: Jcofilms, CC BY 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

What the islands are actually like

Three islands hold 91 percent of the population and the rest is thinly spread. New Providence, which is Nassau, holds 296,732 people, about three-quarters of the country, and effectively all of the specialist healthcare, international schooling, banking and professional services. The western end, around Lyford Cay and Old Fort Bay, is the traditional wealthy expatriate belt.

Grand Bahama, which is Freeport, has 46,740 people and is the only island whose population fell between the 2010 and 2022 censuses, down by 4,628. It also had 4,306 empty dwellings out of 22,127. That is a buyer’s market and a thin one.

The Family Islands are quieter still. Abaco has 16,695 people, Eleuthera 9,104 and Exuma and its cays 7,287. Eleuthera recorded 41 percent of its dwellings vacant at the census. Anyone moving to the Bahamas for an outer island should read that number as both an opportunity and a warning about services.

One change is coming that specifically affects the outer islands. New Providence has historically cross-subsidised Family Island electricity to keep one national tariff, and the current reform explicitly ends that. Family Island residents will move towards paying the true cost of their power.

What things cost

The cost of moving to the Bahamas starts with an inflation rate that is running hot. The statistics institute recorded 4.3 percent in the year to June 2026, easing from 4.5 percent in May and near a three-year peak. The trajectory through the year ran 2.1 percent in January, 3.1 in March, 3.8 in April and 4.5 in May, driven by fuel. Restaurants and hotels were the fastest-rising category all year.

Two other institutions give different numbers for different reasons, and it is worth knowing which you are reading. The central bank reported average inflation of 2.1 percent over the twelve months to April 2026, because it uses a trailing twelve-month average. The International Monetary Fund forecast 1.2 percent for 2026 in January, well below what the monthly series has since delivered.

Value added tax is 10 percent, down from 12 since January 2022, with a reduced 5 percent rate on specified essentials. The cost-of-living change that matters most came on 1 April 2026, when unprepared food sold or imported by a food store became fully exempt: meats, dairy, vegetables, fruit, grains and certain coffee and tea. They had been on the reduced rate since April 2025.

Fuel prices are gazetted under a price control order rather than set by the market, and they carry an explicit island premium. One supplier’s maximum retail price for lead-free petrol was US$7.34 a gallon in New Providence, US$7.39 in Grand Bahama, US$7.52 in Abaco, Andros and Eleuthera and US$7.55 everywhere else, effective 1 June 2026.

The minimum wage is US$6.50 an hour, US$260 for a 40-hour week, and has not moved since January 2023. A review was requested by the national tripartite council on 31 August 2026 and is with the cabinet.

Rent, and the missing index

There is no official rent index in the Bahamas, and this is not an oversight anyone is hiding. The International Monetary Fund’s most recent review of the country says plainly that operationalising real estate price indices is still needed.

So every rent figure in circulation is crowd-sourced, and the samples are thin enough to produce nonsense. One well-known aggregator puts a Nassau one-bedroom at about US$1,490 in the city centre and US$2,000 outside it, which is the wrong way round and a clear sign of a small sample. Another gives US$1,366 and US$970 for the same two categories. A third openly states that Nassau has no independently measured rent baseline.

For Freeport and the Family Islands there is no usable data at all, from any official body, brokerage index or crowd-sourced site. The census vacancy rates are the closest thing to a signal: Grand Bahama 19 percent of dwellings empty, Abaco 27 percent, Eleuthera 41 percent.

The practical advice follows from that. Budget from listings you can see and viewings you make, not from an online average, and expect the range within Nassau to be very wide.

Nassau. There is no official rent index anywhere in the country, and none at all for Freeport or the Family Islands (Photo: Kiran891, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Electricity, water and internet

An electricity bill has a base tariff and a fuel charge. On New Providence and most Family Islands the residential base tariff is free for the first 200 units, then 11.95 cents a unit to 800 and 14.95 cents above that. The fuel charge is a monthly pass-through, and the utility’s own published table shows 17.4 cents below 800 units and 21.4 cents above.

That table appears to stop in February 2026. Bahamian press reporting in June 2026 put fuel above 21 cents and the all-in cost at 33 to 39 cents a unit. The regulator has also found that billed fuel charges never matched actual fuel costs over an 18-month period to March 2024, leaving about US$37.6 million under-recovered. New tariffs are due in 2027, so any figure quoted now carries a known expiry date.

Freeport is the exception and it changed in 2026. Grand Bahama was regulated separately and cost roughly double: the prime minister told Parliament that households using 351 to 800 units paid 22.87 cents there against 11.95 in New Providence. After the government moved to acquire the Grand Bahama utility, rates were cut sharply from the June 2026 billing cycle and the storm recovery charge was abolished.

Water on New Providence is billed from a quarterly minimum of US$36 covering the first 3,000 gallons, then US$12.10 per thousand gallons to 13,000. Family Island residential water starts from a US$18 quarterly minimum.

Internet is published and reveals the island premium again. In Nassau and Abaco, 100 megabits costs US$54.50 a month and a gigabit US$110.50. On the Family Islands the legacy brand offers 30 megabits for US$49.50 — roughly the Nassau price for a fifth of the speed.

Healthcare and hurricanes

Princess Margaret Hospital in Nassau is the main public facility, a teaching hospital with more than 400 beds, the country’s trauma centre and the place where most emergency surgery happens. Rand Memorial serves Freeport. Out Island clinics handle basic outpatient work only.

Doctors Hospital on Collins Avenue is the leading private facility and the only hospital in the country accredited by Joint Commission International, with roughly 70 beds, a 24-hour emergency room, an eight-bed intensive care unit and three theatres.

National health insurance is more generous to foreigners than most such schemes. Under the 2025 act, eligibility extends to anyone ordinarily resident, meaning the Bahamas has been home for at least six months. That person must be either a citizen or a lawful resident under the immigration law, and registered with the national insurance board. Cover is primary care rather than hospital care.

The number that should shape your insurance decision comes from the United States embassy. A medical evacuation to the United States may cost in excess of US$50,000. The patient is responsible for all of it and payment may be demanded in advance, while American public health programmes pay nothing outside the country. On an Out Island that can mean two flights, first to Nassau and then to Florida.

Hurricanes are the other structural risk, and the season runs from 1 June to 30 November. Dorian hit Abaco and Grand Bahama in September 2019 with sustained winds of 185 miles an hour. It caused about US$3.4 billion of economic loss and US$1.5 to 2 billion of insured loss, the largest payout event in Bahamian history. No insurer publishes a rate card, but the industry association said catastrophe premiums rose 30 to 40 percent over the following three to five years.

Tax, banking and safety

There is no income tax, no capital gains tax and no inheritance tax. What there is instead is consumption tax, property tax, stamp duty and business licence fees.

One change on 1 July 2026 matters directly to foreign buyers and is not yet in most guides. The real property tax amendment created a new class, foreign-owned owner-occupied property, taxed at 0.625 percent of assessed value with no exemption on the first US$300,000 and a cap of US$200,000 a year. The exemption and the lower cap are now reserved for Bahamians and for permanent residents with the right to work.

At the other end of the scale, a domestic minimum top-up tax of 15 percent is in force for multinational groups with revenue of 750 million euros or more, enacted in late 2024 and deemed effective from 1 January 2024. It has no bearing on an individual moving over.

Banking is the practical friction. The central bank administers exchange control and applies strict anti-money-laundering rules requiring institutions to know at all times who ultimately benefits from or controls funds in an account. Expect a heavy documentation burden and a slow process.

On safety, Washington keeps the Bahamas at level two, exercise increased caution, renewed on 28 July 2026 with no change to the level. Its language is specific: violent crime can occur anywhere, most of it happens in Nassau and Freeport, and travellers should stay alert in the Over the Hill area of Nassau, south of Shirley Street, where gangs have killed residents. Traffic congestion in Nassau is described as severe, and Bahamians drive on the left.

The Exumas. Out Island clinics handle basic outpatient work only, and anything serious is flown first to Nassau and then often to Florida (Photo: Rüdiger Stehn from Kiel, Deutschland, CC BY-SA 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

Sources: Population and inflation from the Bahamas National Statistical Institute, the peg and exchange control from the Central Bank of The Bahamas, residency thresholds from the Department of Immigration, tariffs from Bahamas Power and Light and the Water and Sewerage Corporation, gazetted fuel prices from the price control orders, tax from the Department of Inland Revenue, and the evacuation and safety warnings from the United States embassy and State Department.

What Is Not Known

What rent costs anywhere in the country. There is no official rent or house price index, and the International Monetary Fund’s own review says such indices still need to be built. The crowd-sourced figures for Nassau contradict each other, including one that puts a one-bedroom outside the centre above one in the centre. For Freeport and the Family Islands there is no usable data at all.

What the electricity fuel charge is right now. The utility’s own published table appears to stop in February 2026 at 17.4 and 21.4 cents a unit, while Bahamian press reporting in June 2026 put fuel above 21 cents and the all-in cost at 33 to 39 cents. New tariffs are due in 2027 in any case.

Whether the remote work permit is still operating. It is still marketed on the tourism ministry’s campaign site with unchanged terms, but it is absent from the immigration department’s own list of permit categories and the application portal did not resolve when checked. No official notice discontinuing or reinstating it could be found.

What property insurance costs. No insurer publishes a rate as a percentage of value or a current deductible schedule. The only figures on the record are the industry association’s statement that catastrophe premiums rose 30 to 40 percent over three to five years, and post-Dorian projections of 15 to 20 percent increases.

The size of the economy. Four official or semi-official figures disagree: a headline nominal GDP of B$17.22 billion for 2025, press-reported advance estimates of B$15.2 billion, a basic prices figure of B$13.83 billion for 2024, and a World Bank market-prices figure of US$15.83 billion for 2024. These are almost certainly different measures and none of them has been reconciled publicly.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is there income tax in the Bahamas?

No. There is no income tax, no capital gains tax and no inheritance tax. The state raises revenue through customs and excise duty on imports, 10 percent value added tax, real property tax, stamp duty and business licence fees, which is why the cost of living is high despite the absence of income tax.

How much money do I need for permanent residence in the Bahamas?

A minimum investment of B$1,000,000, held for at least ten years, either in Bahamian real estate or in zero coupon bonds issued by the central bank. That threshold rose from B$750,000 on 1 January 2025. A separate, higher figure of B$1,500,000 buys accelerated consideration of the application.

Does the Bahamas still have a remote work visa?

Its status is unclear and you should check before relying on it. The Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay is still marketed on the tourism ministry’s campaign site at US$1,025 for a professional and US$525 per dependant, renewable to three years. But it does not appear on the immigration department’s own list of permits, and its application portal did not resolve in late September 2026.

Is healthcare good in the Bahamas?

Nassau is well served by regional standards. Princess Margaret Hospital is the public teaching hospital and trauma centre with more than 400 beds, and Doctors Hospital is the only internationally accredited private hospital in the country. National health insurance covers lawful residents as well as citizens for primary care after six months of residence. The Out Islands have outpatient clinics only.

How much is a medical evacuation from the Bahamas?

The United States embassy says an evacuation to the United States may cost in excess of US$50,000. The patient or their representative is responsible for the whole cost, payment may be required in advance, and American public health programmes pay nothing outside the country. From an Out Island it can mean two flights, first to Nassau.

Where do most foreigners live in the Bahamas?

Overwhelmingly on New Providence, which holds 296,732 people, about three-quarters of the country, and all the specialist healthcare, international schooling and professional services. The western end around Lyford Cay is the traditional expatriate belt. Grand Bahama and the Family Islands are cheaper and far thinner on services, with vacancy rates reaching 41 percent of dwellings on Eleuthera.

World.title: Lego Mexico Investment: US$400 Million for Its Biggest Factory
World.content:
MEXICO · BUSINESS

Key Facts — The country Mexico has about 130 million people and is Latin America’s second-largest economy. Nuevo León is its northern industrial heartland.

— What happened Lego will spend US$400 million expanding its Monterrey-area plant, adding a packaging building and an automated warehouse.

— How big The site already employs up to 6,500 people and made more than 149 million sets in 2025.

— Who announced it Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard and a Lego executive, at President Claudia Sheinbaum’s daily press conference.

— The catch The money is announced, not spent. The work runs to 2029 and the jobs figure is not broken down.

— Why it counts This is Lego’s third Monterrey expansion since 2022, and a bet that North American toys keep being made in Mexico.

The Danish toymaker is pouring more money into a plant that is already the biggest it owns — its third Monterrey expansion since 2022.

The Lego Mexico investment announced on 24 September 2026 is worth US$400 million. It expands the Nuevo León factory that Lego says is its largest anywhere, and adds more than 1,300 jobs.

Monterrey, Nuevo León. Lego’s plant on the city’s northern edge is the group’s largest anywhere (Photo: Daniel Escobedo, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

The plant that is already Lego’s largest

Lego is the Danish company that makes the plastic bricks. Its Mexican factory sits outside Monterrey, the capital of Nuevo León and one of the country’s main industrial cities.

Production there began in 2009. Lego says the site can employ up to 6,500 people.

At the end of 2025 it was the group’s biggest production facility anywhere, by the company’s own account.

The plant makes bricks for the American market. Lego says it produced more than 149 million sets in 2025.

So this is not a company arriving in Mexico. It is a company doubling down on a place it has been for seventeen years.

What the Lego Mexico investment buys

The US$400 million goes into a packaging building and an automated warehouse, alongside further site infrastructure. The work is scheduled to run through 2029.

Lego says the expansion will create more than 1,300 jobs. It has not said how many are permanent production roles and how many are construction.

Packaging and warehousing are unglamorous. They are also what decides how fast finished sets reach shops across North America.

Announced spending is not spent spending. A four-year programme can be slowed, resized or stretched if demand shifts.

Why it was announced from the presidential podium

The announcement came at President Claudia Sheinbaum’s morning press conference, the daily platform her government uses to present investment news.

Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard spoke. Nancy Sánchez, who leads Lego’s manufacturing in the Americas, gave the company’s detail.

That staging is the point. Mexico is competing for manufacturing that might otherwise go to Asia or to the United States itself.

Lego also said more than 90 percent of the inputs it uses in Mexico are bought locally. Host governments like that figure.

Lego did not tie the expansion to trade policy, and neither should a reader. The company has been adding to this site since well before the current tariff argument.

The third expansion, not the first

Lego committed US$500 million to expanding the same Monterrey operation in August 2022, and announced a further expansion in November 2023.

Seen together, the three describe a steady build-out rather than one dramatic bet. The Lego Mexico investment is the latest instalment.

That pattern is more informative than any one number. Companies that keep adding to the same site have usually found the labour and the logistics work.

It also raises the cost of leaving. Each expansion makes the Monterrey complex harder to replace elsewhere.

What a packaging plant says about supply chains

Most manufacturing announcements are about making more things. The Lego Mexico investment is largely about moving them.

An automated warehouse and a packaging building change how fast a finished set reaches a shop shelf.

That matters most for a company selling into the United States. Retail there runs on tight delivery windows and a heavy fourth quarter.

It is also the part of a supply chain that is hardest to relocate. Moulding machines can move; a warehouse built into a site does not.

What it means for people living in or invested in the region

In northern Mexico the effects are local and gradual. Think construction work, supplier contracts, and demand for housing around Monterrey.

For investors, the Lego Mexico investment is a signal about location rather than about Lego. A company with a choice of continents keeps choosing Nuevo León.

It should not be read as a verdict on Mexican trade policy. One company’s four-year plan says little about tariffs, and Lego did not link the two.

Nor does it make Mexico immune to a downturn. Toy demand is consumer demand, and consumer demand turns.

Monterrey’s pull is not mysterious. It has the industrial parks, the road links north, and a labour force that has been building things for a century.

What is still not known

Lego has not broken down the 1,300 jobs. Nor has it said what the plant’s headcount will be when the work ends.

The company has not given a total for what it has now committed to Monterrey across the three expansions.

The exact construction start date was given only in Mexican press reports and was not confirmed in a company document.

Those gaps do not put the announcement in doubt. They simply mean the figures are intentions until the buildings exist.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Lego building a new factory in Mexico?

No — it expands the plant Lego has run outside Monterrey since 2009. The money adds a packaging building and an automated warehouse.

How many jobs will the Lego Mexico investment create?

More than 1,300, on the company’s figure. Lego has not said how many are permanent production roles.

Why does a toy factory matter to investors?

Because of where it is. Lego says the Mexican plant is its largest anywhere, and this is its third Monterrey expansion since 2022.

Sources: https://www.lego.com/en-us/history/articles/i-lego-production-in-mexico; https://politica.expansion.mx/mexico/2026/09/24/lego-inversion-400-millones-dolares-nuevo-leon; https://www.lego.com/en-us/aboutus/news/2022/august/the-lego-group-invests-us-500-million-to-expand-factory-in-monterrey-mexico; https://www.lego.com/en-us/aboutus/news/2023/november/lego-announces-expansion-of-factory-in-monterrey-mexico

World.title: Healthcare in Guyana for Expats 2026: Hospitals, Insurance and the Evacuation Reality
World.content:
GUIDES · GUYANA

Key Facts — What it is A free public system delivered across five levels in ten regions, topped by one national referral hospital in Georgetown, with a small fee-for-service private sector beside it.

— Who it’s for Oil sector staff and contractors, returning diaspora, people posted to Georgetown, and anyone weighing a country whose economy is growing faster than any other on earth.

— What it costs Public care is free, and the health minister says it is delivered regardless of immigration status. Private hospitals and doctors commonly want payment up front, in cash.

— Why it matters Washington describes the quality of medical care as low and inconsistent. London says medical facilities are very limited even in Georgetown, and to arrange evacuation for anything serious or invasive.

— The catch Radiotherapy exists at exactly one site in the country and brachytherapy nowhere, so patients travel. No operator publishes what an evacuation flight costs.

What oil money has actually built, what it has not built yet, and why the most important line in a policy for Guyana is the one about getting you out.

Healthcare in Guyana is being rebuilt in real time and from a low base. Six new regional hospitals opened in 2025, the national referral hospital installed the public system’s first scanner for complex imaging in 2026, and the health budget for the year is 161.1 billion Guyana dollars, about US$773 million. None of that changes what three Western governments still tell their own citizens to plan for.

How the system works

Healthcare in Guyana is organised from the top down. The health ministry in Georgetown sets policy and works through regional health authorities in each of the ten administrative regions, which deliver the care. Services run across five levels, from village health posts up to the national referral hospital, with patients transferred upward when a service is not available locally.

Public care is free, and the constitution treats health as a fundamental right. It is also free to foreigners in practice. The health minister stated the policy plainly: the government delivers healthcare to anyone who needs it at any of its facilities regardless of status, noting that Brazilians cross the border for surgery at Lethem. He added that the position might be revisited if the load became too heavy.

Alongside that sits the National Insurance Scheme, which pays a sickness benefit from the fourth day of incapacity for up to 26 weeks to contributors, and gives its pensioners free prescription drugs plus limited dental and optical care.

A newer scheme subsidises private care. The universal health voucher, launched in March 2025, gives every citizen a 10,000 dollar voucher, about US$48, for a defined panel of laboratory tests at more than 30 participating private providers, where it attracts discounts of 40 to 70 percent.

Georgetown. The national referral hospital, the Cancer Institute and the Caribbean Heart Institute all sit on one campus in the capital (Photo: Ian Mackenzie, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons)

The national referral hospital

Georgetown Public Hospital Corporation, founded in 1838, is the level five referral hospital, the teaching hospital and the research centre. Its own published figures give 558 inpatient beds across 26 wards, 456 doctors and 879 nursing staff, more than 320,000 outpatient visits and 26,600 admissions a year, eleven operating theatres and eight critical care units.

One of those numbers is smaller than the rest and it matters: the accident and emergency department has 19 beds. For a national referral hospital serving a population approaching a million, that is the pinch point.

The government says it has put roughly 85.2 billion dollars, about US$409 million, into the hospital over five years. The 2026 additions are real and checkable. The public system’s first magnetic resonance scanner was installed there in June 2026, alongside a new computed tomography scanner and a catheterisation laboratory in an imaging suite worth around two billion dollars.

Staffing is the weakness the hospital itself concedes. Its chief executive said it is running at more than 60 percent of nursing capacity. Contract nurses have reported going three consecutive months, and in one case eight, without pay because payroll is still processed on paper.

Six new hospitals, and the ones still unbuilt

This is the part of the story that a guide written two years ago would miss.
